body: Hyliion Holdings Corp is a US energy technology company listed on the New York Stock Exchange. It builds the KARNO linear generator and told investors its power modules could serve AI data centers, highlighting a letter of intent worth about $133 million from VFG Holdings for 250 units.

In June 2026, short seller Pelican Way Research published a report on Hyliion, standing to profit if the stock fell. The firm alleged the $133 million letter of intent was misrepresented because VFG Holdings was incorporated in January 2026 and lacked the capacity to support an order of that size. Pelican Way also said CEO Thomas Healy had paid himself more since 2021 than Hyliion generated in total revenue.

The shares had rallied 150% on the letter of intent before collapsing after the report challenged the deal. The $133 million order value and the stock drop are separate amounts: the first was a non-binding purchase figure, and the second was a fall in market price.

On August 11, 2026, Hyliion reported second-quarter earnings, and the stock spiked 26.3% after hours. The gain disappeared by the next trading session, leaving shares at $3.92, 53% below their June high.

title: Deep Fission promised $50 power. A report found costs up to $289.
points: Deep Fission denied the report's doubts about its viability.

body: Deep Fission is a California-based nuclear startup listed on Nasdaq that plans to bury small reactors one mile underground in boreholes. Before its June 2026 initial public offering, the company told investors its reactors would produce power at a levelized cost of $50 to $70 per megawatt-hour.

On September 24, 2026, short seller Iceberg Research published a report and disclosed it held a short position in the stock. Using figures from Deep Fission's own June 2026 prospectus, Iceberg calculated energy costs of $289 per megawatt-hour for the first reactor and $148 for later units, about 200% above prior guidance.

Iceberg also alleged that Deep Fission faced $350 million in unfunded capital needs and that only 4 gigawatts of its claimed 18.5-gigawatt customer pipeline tied to identifiable counterparties under non-binding deals. Deep Fission denied the report's doubts about its viability.

On October 5, 2026, stockholder rights law firm Johnson Fistel announced an investigation into potential securities claims following the report. By October 21, 2026, news reports noted the stock had dropped 50% after the critical report.

title: A 4.6 MB worm file slipped past GitHub code search across 3,000 repositories
points: Starting on June 10, 2026, Deep Specter Research investigated a supply-chain worm called Shai-Hulud using only public data and static-only methods.
The report said the worm used stolen maintainer tokens to commit a roughly 4.6 MB obfuscated file into trusted repositories and forged commit dates to hide the changes.
Deep Specter Research said it found 516 live malicious packages across five ecosystems, more than 3,000 affected GitHub repositories and over 200 compromised developer accounts.
body: GitHub is a software development platform that stores, displays and searches code repositories. It operates a bug disclosure channel on HackerOne where researchers can submit vulnerability reports.

Starting on June 10, 2026, Deep Specter Research investigated a supply-chain worm called Shai-Hulud using only public data and static-only methods. The report said the worm used stolen maintainer tokens to commit a roughly 4.6 MB obfuscated file into trusted repositories and forged commit dates to hide the changes.

The investigators alleged that GitHub code search ignores files that large, hiding the payload from automated scanning while five editor and tool triggers ran the code automatically. Deep Specter Research said it found 516 live malicious packages across five ecosystems, more than 3,000 affected GitHub repositories and over 200 compromised developer accounts.

On June 17, 2026, Deep Specter Research published its findings. The researchers said GitHub had rejected two formal vulnerability reports on these design flaws, closing both as ineligible and not presenting a security risk.

title: AST SpaceMobile missed revenue forecasts by 60% but kept its $200 million target
points: Together, the six companies had a combined market capitalization of $33.2 billion against $361 million in trailing revenue.

body: AST SpaceMobile is a publicly traded space company. It reported $14.7 million in revenue for the first quarter of 2026, against analyst consensus of $37 million, and reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $150 million to $200 million.

On June 12, 2026, Fugazi Research published a short report on six publicly traded space companies. It compared their market values with reported sales. Together, the six companies had a combined market capitalization of $33.2 billion against $361 million in trailing revenue.

Fugazi focused on AST SpaceMobile, which accounted for $295 million of those trailing sales. The company had $3.9 billion in cash and reported a $191 million net loss in the first quarter. Its loss of $0.66 per share exceeded the $0.20 consensus, while its outstanding shares had increased by 69% over the previous year.

Fugazi calculated that AST SpaceMobile's $27.96 billion market capitalization was 140 to 186 times its 2026 revenue guidance. Applying the sector median multiple of 4.4 to the $175 million guidance midpoint implied a $770 million market cap, or 97.2% less. That was a valuation calculation, not a share-price drop.

body: The Ensign Group is a US operator of nursing facilities. It told investors it was focusing on very sick residents to increase government payments. Medicare and Medicaid accounted for 69% of its revenue.

It estimated that 301 Ensign facilities had a staffing gap of 5,248,725 hours, representing $161 million in estimated savings. Hunterbrook reported that its methods had been reviewed by three independent experts. Its affiliated investment firm held a short position in Ensign and a long position in comparable securities when the investigation was published.

title: Five of Rwanda's Seven Largest Coltan Exporters Bought Conflict Minerals

Seven Rwandan companies exported almost 85% of the country's coltan from January 2023 to September 2025.
body: Sony is a Japanese company whose products use minerals found in smartphones and computers. Its supply chain policy requires suppliers to comply with its code of conduct. On June 10, 2026, Global Witness reported that conflict coltan from the Democratic Republic of Congo likely entered Sony's supply chain.

Global Witness spent a year tracing coltan from Rubaya, where 15% of the world's coltan is extracted. Investigators reviewed customs data, trade records and interviews with over 70 people, and travelled with a smuggler past M23 checkpoints.

The report alleged that five of Rwanda's seven biggest coltan exporters bought conflict coltan. Seven Rwandan companies exported almost 85% of the country's coltan from January 2023 to September 2025.

Four traders told investigators that smuggled coltan received ITSCI tags indicating no conflict links. Sony told Global Witness that it expects all suppliers to comply with its supply chain code of conduct and policy.
In early 2026, ITSCI told Global Witness that three additional exporters were under review and at risk of suspension and expulsion. Global Witness published its full report on June 18, 2026.

body: Sports Entertainment Gaming Global, or SEGG Media, is a Nasdaq-listed company that told investors about deals in sports media, lotteries and prediction markets. It published press releases announcing acquisitions, international expansion and a Polymarket deal.

On June 26, 2026, SEGG sued White Diamond Research and Adam Gefvert in Tarrant County District Court in Texas for $20 million in damages. SEGG also announced the launch of prediction market contracts for FIFA World Cup matches through Sports Predicts.

title: Collagen linked to 75,000 hectares of deforestation was sold by Amazon
points: In a separate year-long investigation, Global Witness tracked conflict coltan from the Democratic Republic of Congo across the border into Rwanda, where seven companies exported 85% of the coltan.

body: Amazon is an international retailer that sells consumer products worldwide, including bovine collagen supplements.

Global Witness traced collagen from Paraguay to Rousselot and stated that products containing Rousselot's collagen, including Weider's bovine collagen products, were sold by major retailers such as Amazon and Costco.

In a separate year-long investigation, Global Witness tracked conflict coltan from the Democratic Republic of Congo across the border into Rwanda, where seven companies exported 85% of the coltan. Kerrisdale valued the shares at $17, an 80% drop from trading levels.

body: Affirm Holdings is a Nasdaq-listed Buy Now, Pay Later lender valued at $25 billion. Investors viewed the company as a fast-growing payments platform after its gross merchandise volume grew at 33% a year since 2022.

On January 21, 2026, short seller Kerrisdale Capital published a report on Affirm and disclosed that it held a short position, meaning it profits when the shares fall. The report alleged that Affirm operated like a subprime balance sheet lender rather than a payments facilitator.

Kerrisdale said roughly half of Affirm's revenue came from interest on high-rate installment loans, with an average yield of 31% and its largest loan bucket above 30%. It added that 52% of Affirm's customers had FICO scores below 660, while credit reserves stood at 1% of gross merchandise volume against historical loss rates of 6% to 7%. Kerrisdale valued the shares at $17, an 80% drop from trading levels.
Affirm shares rose 1.8% in morning trading on January 21, 2026, before trading down 0.6% by 12:43 pm Eastern Time that afternoon.

investigator: BMF Reports / BMF Capital, BMF Reports
title: TROOPS Inc. reported $5.2M in cash, then had $14.5M+ in unexplained outflows
points: The firm reviewed SEC filings, Hong Kong court records, auditor history, and offshore entities.
The report alleged a closed-loop structure in which capital recycled internally through circular share transactions, opaque buybacks, and insider-linked entities.
BMF Reports estimated an 80-90% downside risk for the shares.
body: TROOPS Inc. is a Hong Kong company listed on Nasdaq under the ticker TROO. It marketed itself to investors as a diversified fintech and digital services business with exposure to insurance, APIs, blockchain, and software infrastructure.

On January 6, 2026, short seller BMF Reports / BMF Capital published an investigative report and disclosed a short position in the stock, meaning it earns when the shares fall. The firm reviewed SEC filings, Hong Kong court records, auditor history, and offshore entities.

The report alleged a closed-loop structure in which capital recycled internally through circular share transactions, opaque buybacks, and insider-linked entities. It cited $5.2M in reported cash followed by $14.5M+ in unexplained outflows, active winding-up proceedings against subsidiaries, and a core operating unit called APIGuru run by the CEO from a residential address.
BMF Reports estimated an 80-90% downside risk for the shares. On August 28, 2026, BMF Reports listed the same report again on its website.

title: Axis Bank share price fell 4.7% after a meeting with 18 institutional investors
points: The report alleged that the bank shared details about its net interest margin trajectory without releasing the same statement to the stock exchanges.
The Axis Bank share price fell 4.7% on December 16, 2025.
The investigator stated that Axis Bank declined his request to disclose the webcast or transcript of the meeting to the stock exchanges.
body: Axis Bank Limited is a prominent Indian bank and the fifth largest bank by market capitalization. It told investors that its net interest margin was under pressure.

On January 6, 2026, investigator Hemindra Hazari published a report stating that Axis Bank shared price sensitive information at a December 15, 2025 meeting organized by Citi India and attended by 18 institutional participants. The report alleged that the bank shared details about its net interest margin trajectory without releasing the same statement to the stock exchanges.
The Axis Bank share price fell 4.7% on December 16, 2025. Axis Bank neither responded nor uploaded the material to the stock exchanges.
The investigator stated that Axis Bank declined his request to disclose the webcast or transcript of the meeting to the stock exchanges.

title: Cobrapost alleged 10,262 crore rupees in related-party deals at Cholamandalam
points: The report said Cholamandalam had nearly 10,262 crore rupees of transactions between related parties, family members, and key management.
Cobrapost also alleged that Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company diverted 3,040 crore rupees to nine Murugappa Group companies.
It claimed the finance firm earned 942 crore rupees in insurance commissions between 2024 and 2025 and questioned whether it bundled insurance with vehicle loans.
body: Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company is a non-banking financial company in India that is part of the 124-year-old Murugappa Group. A substantial part of its revenues comes from financing vehicles and homes.

On December 22, 2025, the investigative website Cobrapost released a report alleging governance lapses and large-scale related-party transactions at the company. The report said Cholamandalam had nearly 10,262 crore rupees of transactions between related parties, family members, and key management.

Cobrapost also alleged that Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Company diverted 3,040 crore rupees to nine Murugappa Group companies. It claimed the finance firm earned 942 crore rupees in insurance commissions between 2024 and 2025 and questioned whether it bundled insurance with vehicle loans.

On December 23, 2025, Cholamandalam denied the allegations and called them malicious, distorted, and baseless. On December 24, 2025, the company said it would engage with regulators to assess any market-manipulation motive and consult legal advisers about action against Cobrapost.

title: Serve Robotics lost $80 million on $2 million in revenue
points: It found that Serve had lost about $80 million on just $2 million in revenue over the previous twelve months.
It also cited a January incident in which a Miami train struck a robot that had been stuck on the tracks for 15 minutes.
More than 83 percent of respondents strongly opposed allowing delivery robots across the ward.
body: Serve Robotics is a US company that makes self-driving sidewalk robots for food delivery. It presented the robots as a way to cut delivery costs by replacing human couriers and reduce the number of cars on city roads. Investors and analysts expected its revenue to grow 10x in 2026.

On December 18, 2025, The Bear Cave published a report questioning the business model. It found that Serve had lost about $80 million on just $2 million in revenue over the previous twelve months. The report argued that the robots offered a poor solution for food delivery.

The Bear Cave spent hours watching Serve robots in Brickell. It cited footage of a robot forcing its way through restaurant seating. The supplied accounts did not give the share-price change on the report date or a company response.

On March 5, 2026, The Bear Cave published another report. It said several restaurants had stopped working with Serve or remained in testing. It also cited a January incident in which a Miami train struck a robot that had been stuck on the tracks for 15 minutes.

The March report also cited a Chicago ward survey by Alderman Daniel La Spata. More than 83 percent of respondents strongly opposed allowing delivery robots across the ward. La Spata concluded that Serve and its competitor should not have a long-term presence there.

title: Via Transportation got about 72% of revenue from services, not software
points: The report alleged that about 72% of Via's revenue came from services driven by driver hours and vehicle use, rather than software.
It said software fees were typically less than 5% of contract values.
The report claimed that Via excluded insurance expenses from cost of revenue and classified support costs under general expenses, overstating gross margins by an estimated 3-4%.
body: Via Transportation is a public transit contractor that sells transport services and software to local governments. The recently listed company presented itself as a software-driven platform, with a market value of about $2.4 billion.

On December 16, 2025, Bleecker Street Research published a report after reviewing more than 400 public procurement processes and over 100 signed government contracts. It also interviewed former employees, competitors and local officials. Funds managed by Bleecker Street held a short position in Via, which stood to gain if its shares fell.

The report alleged that about 72% of Via's revenue came from services driven by driver hours and vehicle use, rather than software. It said software fees were typically less than 5% of contract values. Bleecker Street also alleged that Via collected implementation fees and up to 18 months of software charges upfront, inflating its reported annual recurring revenue.

The report claimed that Via excluded insurance expenses from cost of revenue and classified support costs under general expenses, overstating gross margins by an estimated 3-4%. It also cited LA Metro reducing prices or replacing Via software and former employees who linked about 10-20% of customer losses to expiring grants.
Bleecker Street valued Via shares at $11.80, implying 60% downside.

title: RadNet touted 30% AI growth. Half its same-center gains came from closing sites.
points: The report alleged that Digital Health brought in less than 5% of revenue, about $65 million out of $1.5 billion in the first nine months of 2025, mostly from sales to RadNet's own clinics.
Hunterbrook estimated that about half of reported same-center growth came from closing centers within 15 minutes of surviving sites, cutting organic growth to an estimated 2.5% to 3%.
Insiders also sold more than 780,000 shares for $50.9 million over two years.
body: RadNet is a US chain of medical imaging centers that told investors it was growing fast through artificial intelligence. It reported 30% year-over-year revenue growth in its Digital Health segment and 6% to 10% same-center sales growth.

In December 2025, Hunterbrook Media published an investigation while its affiliate, Hunterbrook Capital, held a short position, which profits if shares fall. Hunterbrook tracked RadNet's locations and analyzed its filings.
The report alleged that Digital Health brought in less than 5% of revenue, about $65 million out of $1.5 billion in the first nine months of 2025, mostly from sales to RadNet's own clinics.

Hunterbrook estimated that about half of reported same-center growth came from closing centers within 15 minutes of surviving sites, cutting organic growth to an estimated 2.5% to 3%. Insiders also sold more than 780,000 shares for $50.9 million over two years.
RadNet did not reply and did not dispute the findings. In its 2025 10-K filing, RadNet removed the phrase same-center completely, down from 18 mentions in its 2024 10-K.

title: Ceres Power shares rose over 250%. Its partnerships came under scrutiny.
points: The short seller, which stood to gain if the shares fell, examined the company's partnerships and commercial history from 2013 through 2023.
The report also questioned Ceres' relationship with Weichai, its biggest shareholder, alleging repeated failures to bring joint products to market since 2018.
Alliance News separately reported shares trading 7.6% lower at 285.20 pence.
body: Ceres Power Holdings is a UK developer of technology that turns fuel into electricity and uses electricity to produce hydrogen. It relies on manufacturing partners to bring its technology to market. Its shares had risen more than 250% since partner Doosan Fuel Cell announced the start of its systems at a new 50MW factory in July 2025.

On December 11, 2025, Grizzly Research published a report alleging that Ceres used major partnership announcements to support expectations of future sales. The short seller, which stood to gain if the shares fell, examined the company's partnerships and commercial history from 2013 through 2023.

Grizzly alleged that repeated agreements had failed to produce lasting commercial products or meaningful revenue. It pointed to Bosch, which had acquired nearly 18% of Ceres and committed over €400 million to production before the partnership ended in early 2025.

The report also questioned Ceres' relationship with Weichai, its biggest shareholder, alleging repeated failures to bring joint products to market since 2018. Grizzly argued that Ceres shifted product development and factory investment costs onto partners. Ceres shares fell more than 15% after the report. Alliance News separately reported shares trading 7.6% lower at 285.20 pence.

title: Advance Auto Parts owed banks money recorded as supplier bills
points: The firm said Advance Auto Parts continued to lose market share and sales despite its efforts to improve operations.
J Capital alleged that the company's debt was higher than it appeared.
It said most accounts payable, normally bills owed to suppliers, were actually debts to banks through supplier factoring.
body: Advance Auto Parts is a US retailer of replacement car parts. In 2025, it raised cash, extended debt maturities, sold assets and cut costs to ease pressure on its finances. It had already gone through two major restructuring programs.

On December 10, 2025, J Capital Research published a report questioning the retailer's financial position. The firm said Advance Auto Parts continued to lose market share and sales despite its efforts to improve operations. It compared the retailer with AutoZone and O'Reilly Automotive.

J Capital alleged that the company's debt was higher than it appeared. It said most accounts payable, normally bills owed to suppliers, were actually debts to banks through supplier factoring. Under that arrangement, banks finance supplier payments, leaving the retailer owing the banks.

The report also pointed to high interest payments on existing bonds, which J Capital expected to rise further. It suspected that Advance Auto Parts was paying additional, undisclosed financing costs on inventory. The firm warned that less favorable supplier credit from banks could make buying replacement parts harder.
The report described the company's measures to raise cash and reduce financial pressure but argued that its remaining options were limited.

title: SES AI forecast up to $45 million from a deal staff never spoke of again
points: The report alleged that SES AI promoted phantom deals and an AI product resembling a ChatGPT wrapper to distract from losing major customers Honda and Hyundai, which Wolfpack estimated accounted for 74% of sales that year.
The report also alleged that SES AI's September acquisition of Chinese firm UZ Energy involved a US entity whose registered agent settled a case over a $1 billion Ponzi scheme.
Shares of SES AI fell 5% on December 9, 2025, after the report came out.
body: SES AI is a US-listed company developing lithium metal batteries and an AI platform called Molecular Universe. In February 2025, it told investors a non-binding deal with Texas energy provider AISPEX would generate up to $45 million in revenue in 2025 and beyond.

On December 9, 2025, Wolfpack Research published a report on SES AI and disclosed a short position, meaning it earns when the shares fall. The report alleged that SES AI promoted phantom deals and an AI product resembling a ChatGPT wrapper to distract from losing major customers Honda and Hyundai, which Wolfpack estimated accounted for 74% of sales that year.

Wolfpack reviewed company filings and spoke with a former SES employee, who said the AISPEX announcement was a complete surprise and staff did nothing to fulfill it. The report also alleged that SES AI's September acquisition of Chinese firm UZ Energy involved a US entity whose registered agent settled a case over a $1 billion Ponzi scheme.
Shares of SES AI fell 5% on December 9, 2025, after the report came out.

title: Nvidia said China sales went to zero. Short sellers said over 20% remained.
points: Culper reviewed financial statements and interviewed former employees, alleging over 20% of Nvidia's FY 2026 compute revenues remained driven by China through Southeast Asian buyers such as Megaspeed and OBON Corp.
U.S. prosecutors indicted three Super Micro Computer employees for illegally selling approximately $2.5 billion of servers with Nvidia chips to China via a Southeast Asian front company.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang abruptly resigned on November 12, 2026, and agreed to answer questions from three House committees on December 1, 2026.
body: Nvidia is a listed chipmaker that told investors its business in China went to zero after April 2025 U.S. trade restrictions.

On May 13, 2026, short seller Culper Research published a report saying it held a short position, earning when the shares fall. Culper reviewed financial statements and interviewed former employees, alleging over 20% of Nvidia's FY 2026 compute revenues remained driven by China through Southeast Asian buyers such as Megaspeed and OBON Corp.

In March 2026, U.S. prosecutors indicted three Super Micro Computer employees for illegally selling approximately $2.5 billion of servers with Nvidia chips to China via a Southeast Asian front company. On November 17, 2026, short seller Muddy Waters Research disclosed a short position and raised questions about ties between former Nvidia executive Jay Puri and former Super Micro executive Cenly Chen.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang abruptly resigned on November 12, 2026, and agreed to answer questions from three House committees on December 1, 2026.

title: Short sellers claimed up to 40% of Sportradar's revenue came from illegal betting
points: The report pointed to logos for Stake and 188Bet in Sportradar's April 2025 investor presentation, noting 188Bet was licensed in Anjouan and Stake operated in legally ambiguous territories.
Callisto Research said it found more than 270 operators using Sportradar products illegally and cited a former employee who estimated 30% to 40% of revenue came from them.
Sportradar shares fell about 20% following the April reports.
body: Sportradar Group is a Switzerland-based sports technology company that sells sports data and betting software to sportsbooks. It told investors it was the global leader in sports technology with data distribution across 400 sporting bodies and 800 betting operators.

On November 20, 2025, short seller The Bear Cave published a report alleging that Sportradar facilitated crooked gambling and serviced grey market operators. The report pointed to logos for Stake and 188Bet in Sportradar's April 2025 investor presentation, noting 188Bet was licensed in Anjouan and Stake operated in legally ambiguous territories. Sportradar shares fell 5.9% that day.

By April 26, 2026, two other short sellers had published reports on Sportradar. Callisto Research said it found more than 270 operators using Sportradar products illegally and cited a former employee who estimated 30% to 40% of revenue came from them. Hours later, Muddy Waters Research estimated illegal operators delivered about 20% to 40% of total revenues.

Sportradar shares fell about 20% following the April reports. The company denied the claims, saying the reports showed a misunderstanding of its business and were written by short sellers trying to profit from stock disruption.

title: 36% of Praxis trial patients quit treatment. Their results were modeled.
points: Culper said 36% of treated patients had discontinued, while 81% of pooled dropouts occurred early.
In its November 20 report, Culper disputed Praxis's 2.5-point sensitivity test and stood by its allegations.
A later listing on November 21, 2025, reported the short-seller allegations.
body: Praxis Precision Medicines is a US drug developer testing ulixacaltamide, or ulixa, for essential tremor. In October 2025, it announced positive Phase 3 trial results. The company then raised $567 million in capital.

On November 20, 2025, Culper Research, which held a short position in Praxis, challenged those results. Culper interviewed former Praxis directors, a biostatistician and four former FDA officials. It alleged that Praxis had used statistical modeling to turn missing patient results into evidence of a treatment benefit.

In September 2025, Praxis had moved the trial's primary measurement date from Day 84 to Day 56. Culper said 36% of treated patients had discontinued, while 81% of pooled dropouts occurred early. It argued that the earlier endpoint and assumptions about missing results had made the treatment appear more effective.

Praxis CEO Souza defended the endpoint change and the company's statistical methods. Praxis maintained that the trial was successful regardless of the endpoint change. The supplied accounts gave no share-price movement for November 20, 2025.

In its November 20 report, Culper disputed Praxis's 2.5-point sensitivity test and stood by its allegations. A later listing on November 21, 2025, reported the short-seller allegations. That listing also referenced subsequent FDA acceptance of ulixacaltamide, without providing an acceptance date.

investigator: Gotham City Research, J Capital Research
title: Iron Mountain claimed a 60% dividend payout ratio. A report estimated it over 200%.
points: The report alleged that actual leverage was 9x, or 8.7x to 8.9x, and that the dividend payout ratio had typically exceeded 200% over the past 12 years.
Gotham City Research valued the shares at $23 to $41, implying a 54% to 74% drop.
Iron Mountain shares fell 6% on November 19, 2025.
body: Iron Mountain is a United States document storage company listed on the New York Stock Exchange. It told investors that its adjusted EBITDA margins were improving, its leverage was 5x, and its dividend payout ratio was 60%.

On November 19, 2025, short seller Gotham City Research published a report on the company. It estimated that Iron Mountain overstated adjusted EBITDA by 25% to 35% by adding back restructuring costs and understating recurring capital spending at $140 million instead of $300 million to $350 million a year.

The report alleged that actual leverage was 9x, or 8.7x to 8.9x, and that the dividend payout ratio had typically exceeded 200% over the past 12 years. It also said the SEC had questioned the company's adjusted EBITDA calculations in correspondence letters earlier that year, and that 40 executives had left since March 2024 while insiders sold $215 million of stock.
Gotham City Research valued the shares at $23 to $41, implying a 54% to 74% drop. Iron Mountain shares fell 6% on November 19, 2025.

title: Critical Metals claimed 75% magnet oxides. Its filings showed about 27%.
points: Short seller NINGI Research published a report after reviewing the company's filings, technical reports, and Preliminary Economic Assessment.
It said the actual heavy rare earth oxide content at Tanbreez was only about 27%.
The report alleged that the company's economic model claimed 100% of final processed product revenue while leaving out 100% of processing costs for an unprocessable mineral.
body: Critical Metals Corp is a Nasdaq-listed company promoting two mining projects. It told investors that 75% of the rare earth oxides at its Tanbreez project were magnet oxides and called its Wolfsberg site Europe's first fully permitted lithium mine.

On November 18, 2025, short seller NINGI Research published a report after reviewing the company's filings, technical reports, and Preliminary Economic Assessment. It said the actual heavy rare earth oxide content at Tanbreez was only about 27%.

The report alleged that the company's economic model claimed 100% of final processed product revenue while leaving out 100% of processing costs for an unprocessable mineral. It also said Austrian mining authorities had confirmed that core mining and construction permits for Wolfsberg were not granted, and that every public company tied to chief executive Tony Sage had fallen 91% to 100% or been delisted.

title: SpongeBob SquarePants applied to Perdoceo's university. Its enrollment rose 28%.
points: The report alleged that weak identity checks let automated ghost students enroll with little human oversight beyond phone screenings.
Using industry estimates of 5% to 15% ghost student enrollment, Bleecker Street estimated that fraud accounted for about 8% of Perdoceo's revenue and 34% of its operating income.
In a follow-up report, Bleecker Street forecast that Perdoceo's enrollments would decline by about 7% and earnings would fall about 20%, setting a share price target of $14 to $16.
body: Perdoceo Education is a for-profit education company listed on Nasdaq. Its largest school, Colorado Technical University, reported enrollment growth peaking at 28% year-over-year in the first quarter of 2024. On earnings calls in 2024 and 2025, management told investors this growth came from student engagement and generative AI recruiting.

On November 17, 2025, short seller Bleecker Street Research published a report on Perdoceo and disclosed that its managed funds were short the stock. To test admission controls, the researchers applied to Colorado Technical University using fictional identities, including SpongeBob SquarePants with a Krusty Krab email address.

The report alleged that weak identity checks let automated ghost students enroll with little human oversight beyond phone screenings. Using industry estimates of 5% to 15% ghost student enrollment, Bleecker Street estimated that fraud accounted for about 8% of Perdoceo's revenue and 34% of its operating income.
In a follow-up report, Bleecker Street forecast that Perdoceo's enrollments would decline by about 7% and earnings would fall about 20%, setting a share price target of $14 to $16.

title: Better Home & Finance lost $206 million in 2024 on $108 million of revenue
points: Short seller Deep Credit Research predicted the company would continuously issue new equity to maintain its current level of mortgage lending.
Deep Credit Research had raised concerns about a recent chief financial officer departure and potential liquidity issues.
Another commentator, George Noble, noted on October 9, 2026, that the company lost $206 million in 2024 on $108 million of revenue and had lost more than $1.5 billion since 2022.
body: Better Home & Finance Holding Company is a mortgage origination company listed on Nasdaq under the ticker BETR. It told investors it maintained a low-risk model by selling originated loans to a network of more than 45 investors after holding them for about 22 days.

In November 2025, short seller Deep Credit Research predicted the company would continuously issue new equity to maintain its current level of mortgage lending. On December 16, 2025, Deep Credit Research published another report examining leverage ratios, at-the-money issuance and insider sales by company officers, stating it held a short position in BETR and would gain if the shares fell.

Deep Credit Research had raised concerns about a recent chief financial officer departure and potential liquidity issues. Another commentator, George Noble, noted on October 9, 2026, that the company lost $206 million in 2024 on $108 million of revenue and had lost more than $1.5 billion since 2022.
On March 26, 2026, Better Home & Finance and Coinbase launched a product allowing borrowers to pledge Bitcoin or USDC as down payment collateral on a Fannie Mae conforming mortgage.

title: IperionX Was Valued at $1.2 Billion Without Historical Revenue
points: The report said IperionX had few customer contracts and no historical revenue, despite a $1.2 billion market capitalization.
Spruce Point calculated that IperionX traded at 9.7 times book value and 24 times estimated 2026 revenue, compared with industry medians of 1.4 and 1.8 times.
The report estimated potential share-price downside of 70% to 95% under certain scenarios.
body: IperionX Ltd is an Australian company listed on Nasdaq and the ASX that aims to produce titanium powder and products, from mining through manufacturing. It promoted its HAMR technology as a way to replace the established Kroll process and produce titanium at lower cost.

On November 12, 2025, Spruce Point Capital Management published a forensic review questioning the company's valuation and plans to expand production. The report said IperionX had few customer contracts and no historical revenue, despite a $1.2 billion market capitalization.

Spruce Point calculated that IperionX traded at 9.7 times book value and 24 times estimated 2026 revenue, compared with industry medians of 1.4 and 1.8 times. It questioned whether HAMR could operate at scale using titanium scrap and said the alternative Titan mining project in Tennessee had fallen behind its initial timeline.
The report estimated potential share-price downside of 70% to 95% under certain scenarios. That was a forecast, not an actual market loss.

On November 17, 2025, IperionX responded that its technologies had received support through multiple U.S. evaluations. It said Spruce Point had neither contacted management nor visited or requested access to its Virginia manufacturing operations, and reaffirmed its focus on scaling production there.

title: Meta boosted capital spending by 73% while preparing layoffs for tens of thousands
points: Meta struck a $27 billion financing deal with Blue Owl Capital for a data center in Louisiana, retaining about 20% equity.
It spent $72.22 billion in capital outlays in 2025 and boosted its annual capital spending plans by 73% on January 28, 2026.
That day, fourth-quarter advertising revenue rose to $58.14 billion from $46.78 billion the previous year, and shares rose 10% in extended trading.
body: Meta is a social media company that owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. On November 7, 2025, it told investors it would invest $600 billion in U.S. infrastructure and jobs over the next three years to build artificial intelligence data centers.

On October 21, 2025, Meta struck a $27 billion financing deal with Blue Owl Capital for a data center in Louisiana, retaining about 20% equity. It spent $72.22 billion in capital outlays in 2025 and boosted its annual capital spending plans by 73% on January 28, 2026.

That day, fourth-quarter advertising revenue rose to $58.14 billion from $46.78 billion the previous year, and shares rose 10% in extended trading. The capital spending increase and the share price rise are separate amounts: the first is company outlays, and the second is stock value.

On April 9, 2026, Reuters reported on an internal memo showing Meta was drafting software engineers into a new AI engineering organization. Reuters reported the reorganization came as Meta planned layoffs that could eliminate tens of thousands of jobs to offset its artificial intelligence infrastructure costs.

title: Davis Commodities pitched AI and blockchain with less than $1 million in the bank
points: The report stated that audited numbers showed margins under 2%, negative cash flow, and less than $1 million in the bank, with one family controlling 70% to 75% of the vote.
Three days later, on November 10, 2025, BMF Reports published its own report and stated it held a short position in the stock.
Both reports remain listed on BMF Reports' website as of August 28, 2026.
body: Davis Commodities is a Singapore-based agricultural commodity trader that listed on Nasdaq in 2023. It presented itself to investors as an asset-light, high-growth exporter of sugar, rice, and oils across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East, and promoted a shift toward AI-powered trading, blockchain-driven digital finance, and digital-ESG innovation.

On November 7, 2025, Fugazi Research published a report on the company based on public information, independent research, and interviews. The report stated that audited numbers showed margins under 2%, negative cash flow, and less than $1 million in the bank, with one family controlling 70% to 75% of the vote.

Three days later, on November 10, 2025, BMF Reports published its own report and stated it held a short position in the stock. BMF Reports alleged that the company was a manufactured narrative rather than a trade finance business, and valued the stock at no more than $0.30 per share, representing a 95% downside from its trading level at the time.
Fugazi Research disclosed that it and its affiliates may hold long or short positions in the securities discussed. Both reports remain listed on BMF Reports' website as of August 28, 2026.

title: A contractor lent her licenses for a 3-percent fee and returned P15 million
points: Auditors said many projects were awarded to a small group of contractors identified in Malacanang's review, including SYMS Construction Trading.
A week later, Santos returned P15 million to the government.
The P31.03 billion in projects went to Discaya-linked companies, while the P15 million was the amount Santos returned.
body: SYMS Construction Trading is a Philippine construction firm owned and managed by Sally Santos.

The Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism reported that companies linked to Pacifico "Curlee" and Cezarah "Sarah" Discaya secured 421 flood-control projects worth P31.03 billion from 2022 to 2025. Auditors said many projects were awarded to a small group of contractors identified in Malacanang's review, including SYMS Construction Trading.

The Senate summoned and questioned owners of those firms in multiple hearings. During legislative inquiries, Santos admitted she had lent her contractor's licenses to DPWH engineers for use in projects in exchange for a 3-percent royalty fee.
A week later, Santos returned P15 million to the government. The P31.03 billion in projects went to Discaya-linked companies, while the P15 million was the amount Santos returned.

title: HelloFresh spent €100 million on buybacks while its CEO pledged 77% of his shares
points: By examining corporate filings, balance sheets, and web traffic data, Grizzly Research alleged that Google searches for HelloFresh fell 80% and website traffic dropped over 61%.
The report also alleged that HelloFresh burned about €100 million on share buybacks in 2025 while the stock fell about 50%.
Grizzly Research calculated that CEO Dominik Richter had pledged 77% of his HelloFresh shares as loan collateral through his private firm, DSR Ventures.
body: HelloFresh SE is a German meal-kit company that delivers pre-portioned ingredients and recipe cards to subscribers each week. Its revenue peaked at €7.6 billion in 2022 and later flatlined.

On November 6, 2025, short seller Grizzly Research published a report saying it stood to gain if HelloFresh shares fell. By examining corporate filings, balance sheets, and web traffic data, Grizzly Research alleged that Google searches for HelloFresh fell 80% and website traffic dropped over 61%.

The report also alleged that HelloFresh burned about €100 million on share buybacks in 2025 while the stock fell about 50%. Grizzly Research calculated that CEO Dominik Richter had pledged 77% of his HelloFresh shares as loan collateral through his private firm, DSR Ventures.

The buyback spending and the drop in share price are different amounts: the company spent the cash, while shareholders held the falling stock. On November 6, 2025, German financial newspapers reported that HelloFresh shares plunged after the report.

On November 10, 2025, WirtschaftsWoche reported that HelloFresh pushed back against the short seller as its shares fell. On September 25, 2026, Börsen-Zeitung reported that HelloFresh had still not emerged from its difficulties.

title: GPGI shares fell 44% after a short seller alleged a 90% cash flow overstatement
points: The report alleged that GPGI had overstated Husky's value to win shareholder approval for the deal and overstated free cash flow by 90%.
GPGI released fourth-quarter and fiscal year 2025 results disclosing that Husky's EBITDA declined 5.4% year-over-year in the quarter and 3% for the full year.
Between February 26, 2026 and May 7, 2026, GPGI's stock price fell from $23.12 to $12.94 per share, a drop of approximately 44%.
body: GPGI, Inc., formerly known as CompoSecure, Inc., is listed on the NYSE under the ticker GPGI. On January 12, 2026, the company announced it had completed the acquisition of Husky Technologies Limited and rebranded as GPGI.

On February 26, 2026, short seller Jehoshaphat Research published a report on the company and said it held a short position, meaning it earns when the shares fall. The report alleged that GPGI had overstated Husky's value to win shareholder approval for the deal and overstated free cash flow by 90%.

On March 12, 2026, GPGI released fourth-quarter and fiscal year 2025 results disclosing that Husky's EBITDA declined 5.4% year-over-year in the quarter and 3% for the full year. Between February 26, 2026 and May 7, 2026, GPGI's stock price fell from $23.12 to $12.94 per share, a drop of approximately 44%.

By July 28, 2026, law firms Robbins LLP and the Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz announced securities class action lawsuits on behalf of shareholders who bought GPGI stock between November 3, 2025 and May 6, 2026.

title: Mailisa Beauty Clinic distributed over 8 million products. Police banned 162 of them.
points: Hanoi police inspected the clinic and VietNamNet reported on the case.
Authorities also seized 300 taels of gold, 100 land use certificates, and 3 billion VND.
The Criminal Police Department confirmed that the owners had paid approximately 300 billion VND, or around $12 million, to mitigate consequences in the criminal investigation.
body: Mailisa Beauty Clinic Co., Ltd. is a Vietnamese beauty chain that specialized in skincare and cosmetic procedures. It expanded to 17 branches nationwide and distributed over 8 million cosmetic products under the Doctor Magic brand across nearly 100 product codes.

In November 2025, Hanoi police inspected the clinic and VietNamNet reported on the case. Police alleged that the company's owners smuggled low-quality cosmetics from China into Vietnam using fake labels and foreign fronts, earning illicit profits worth trillions of Vietnamese dong.

On November 21, 2025, the Investigative Police Agency of the Ministry of Public Security prosecuted and detained Director Phan Thi Mai and General Director Hoang Kim Khanh on charges of smuggling. Authorities also seized 300 taels of gold, 100 land use certificates, and 3 billion VND.

On November 25, 2025, the Drug Administration of Vietnam recalled 80 product registration numbers and suspended the circulation of 162 cosmetic products nationwide linked to the chain. On December 15, 2025, the Criminal Police Department confirmed that the owners had paid approximately 300 billion VND, or around $12 million, to mitigate consequences in the criminal investigation.

title: Datavault AI touted a $150 million deal and an AI center. A short seller questioned both.
points: It also noted that chief executive Nathaniel Bradley had faced a July 2021 SEC charge, a $40,000 fine, and a three-year penny-stock bar.

body: Datavault AI is a Nasdaq-listed data tokenization and management company. It told investors it operated a blockchain-powered platform and had opened a Center for AI and Quantum, while announcing partnerships including a $150 million deal and a $2 million fee agreement.

On October 31, 2025, Wolfpack Research published a report and disclosed a short position in the stock. The report alleged that platform trading was minimal or non-existent, that partners had limited cash, and that people asked about the claimed centers said no such thing existed. It also noted that chief executive Nathaniel Bradley had faced a July 2021 SEC charge, a $40,000 fine, and a three-year penny-stock bar.
Datavault AI shares fell $0.49, or 19.44%, to close at $2.03 on October 31, 2025. The company denied the claims, sent a cease-and-desist demand, and said it intended to sue Wolfpack Research.
A securities class action lawsuit was later filed against Datavault AI in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania, with a lead-plaintiff deadline of October 5, 2026.

title: Cobrapost alleged Rs 41,921 crore was diverted through Reliance Group companies
points: Investigative journalism platform Cobrapost alleged that Anil Ambani’s Reliance Group had diverted more than Rs 41,921 crore since 2006.
It said about Rs 28,874 crore raised through loans, share offerings and bonds was siphoned from listed companies to promoter-linked businesses.
The group reported that Reliance Power and Reliance Infrastructure had lost over Rs 15,000 crore in combined market value over the preceding three months, not necessarily on publication day.
body: Anil Ambani’s Reliance Group included listed companies Reliance Power and Reliance Infrastructure. The group raised money through bank loans, public share offerings and bonds, while its companies operated under the Reliance name.

On October 30, 2025, investigative journalism platform Cobrapost alleged that Anil Ambani’s Reliance Group had diverted more than Rs 41,921 crore since 2006. It said about Rs 28,874 crore raised through loans, share offerings and bonds was siphoned from listed companies to promoter-linked businesses.

Cobrapost said it traced money through dozens of subsidiaries, shell companies and special purpose vehicles. It identified 26 offshore beneficiary entities and described routes through the British Virgin Islands, Cyprus, Mauritius, the United States, the United Kingdom and Singapore, including transfers toward Reliance Innoventures.

Reliance Group denied the allegations and called the report a motivated campaign to manipulate share prices. It said authorities including the CBI, ED and SEBI had already examined the information. The group reported that Reliance Power and Reliance Infrastructure had lost over Rs 15,000 crore in combined market value over the preceding three months, not necessarily on publication day.
On October 31, 2025, Reliance Group sought regulatory scrutiny of recent trading activity. It maintained that the allegations were false and that Cobrapost's campaign had damaged its reputation.

title: Cobrapost alleged a Rs. 28,874 crore diversion at Reliance ADA Group
points: The report said they routed loans and investor money through domestic pass-through firms, special purpose vehicles, and 26 offshore entities to Reliance Innoventures.
28,874 crore figure is the amount allegedly siphoned out, while the $1.53 billion figure is the amount allegedly brought in from overseas.
Reliance ADA Group denied all allegations on October 30, 2025, calling the report false, baseless, and a malicious campaign meant to crash its share prices.
body: Reliance ADA Group is an Indian conglomerate led by Anil Ambani and his family with businesses in telecom, financial services, power, and infrastructure. Its listed entities raised funds from public sector banks, bonds, and initial public offerings.

On October 30, 2025, the Indian news website Cobrapost published a report alleging that group companies diverted about Rs. 28,874 crore since 2006. The report said they routed loans and investor money through domestic pass-through firms, special purpose vehicles, and 26 offshore entities to Reliance Innoventures.

Cobrapost also alleged that $1.53 billion, or about Rs. 13,047.50 crore, entered the companies from abroad in a dubious manner. The Rs. 28,874 crore figure is the amount allegedly siphoned out, while the $1.53 billion figure is the amount allegedly brought in from overseas.

Reliance ADA Group denied all allegations on October 30, 2025, calling the report false, baseless, and a malicious campaign meant to crash its share prices. The group stated that related matters were pending before the Central Bureau of Investigation and the Enforcement Directorate.

title: A battery maker kept three financial models and hid toxic gas leaks
points: The report also alleged that Eos Energy battery packs leaked toxic hydrogen bromide gas during thermal events, exceeded safety limits, and achieved 42% to 55% round-trip efficiency.

body: Eos Energy is a zinc-bromide battery maker listed on Nasdaq. The company pitched its batteries as safer than lithium-ion technology and advertised a 75% round-trip efficiency.

On October 30, 2025, short seller Fuzzy Panda Research published a report on Eos Energy and disclosed a short position in its stock. Using public records requests and interviews with customers and former executives, the investigator alleged that Eos Energy kept three sets of financial models and sent inflated projections to the Department of Energy to secure a $90.9 million loan.

The report also alleged that Eos Energy battery packs leaked toxic hydrogen bromide gas during thermal events, exceeded safety limits, and achieved 42% to 55% round-trip efficiency. It further alleged that about 80% of the company's order backlog was worthless and that the batteries cost more to produce than their selling price.
Fuzzy Panda Research stated that sending false statements to the Department of Energy could trigger a default and make the $90.9 million loan immediately payable.

title: DHFL allegedly lent Rs 31,000 crore to entities linked to its promoters
points: Cobrapost's October 30, 2025 investigation also named Wadhawan-controlled DHFL among business groups involved in alleged fund diversion.
Wadhawan said DHFL was in advanced stages of selling non-core assets and expected to generate Rs 4,000-5,000 crore in liquidity over the next 4-5 months.
Cobrapost's October 30, 2025 report subsequently included DHFL among the groups it examined.
body: Dewan Housing Finance (DHFL) was a housing finance company. Its chairman and managing director, Kapil Wadhawan, told investors that the company was working to sell assets outside its main business to raise cash and meet its liabilities.

Cobrapost accused DHFL of giving Rs 31,000 crore in loans to entities it described as dubious and linked to the company's promoters. The investigator alleged that those promoters were the ultimate beneficiaries of the funds.

Cobrapost's October 30, 2025 investigation also named Wadhawan-controlled DHFL among business groups involved in alleged fund diversion. It described the use of pass-through entities, subsidiaries and offshore companies in transactions involving the ADA Group, but did not establish that DHFL used the same routes.

DHFL denied the Cobrapost allegations. Its shares were trading 4 per cent lower on Wednesday as the company responded. The share price decline was separate from the Rs 31,000 crore in loans questioned by Cobrapost.

Wadhawan said DHFL was in advanced stages of selling non-core assets and expected to generate Rs 4,000-5,000 crore in liquidity over the next 4-5 months. The company said asset sales would generate capital without diluting shareholders. Cobrapost's October 30, 2025 report subsequently included DHFL among the groups it examined.

title: Anavex sold a potential Alzheimer drug for a decade while trial endpoints changed

body: Anavex Life Sciences is a United States company that told investors its flagship molecule blarcamesine was a potential disease-modifying therapy for Alzheimer’s and other central-nervous-system disorders.

On October 29, 2025, short seller BMF Reports published a report and said it was short the stock. The report alleged that the company manipulated trial endpoints, including a quiet endpoint switch for RSBQ AUC, and cited a failed functional endpoint with ADCS-ADL p=0.36.

body: Ducommun is a US aerospace and defense company that sold investors a story of revenue growth.

title: RXO reported 16-19% gross margins. A short seller alleged it had $7 million in cash.
points: The firm analyzed public filings and alleged that RXO shifted costs of revenue to operating expenses to report 16-19% margins while industry peers made 6-8%.
It also alleged that RXO changed its definition of EBITDA to avoid breaching debt covenants after cash fell to $7 million.
In a filing on January 23, 2026, RXO announced that Chief Accounting Officer Jason Kerr would retire on May 15, 2026.
body: RXO, Inc. is a US digital freight brokerage that spun off from XPO. The company told investors its business generated strong performance and 16-19% gross margins.

On October 22, 2025, DF Research, led by Keith Dalrymple, published a report and disclosed a position in the securities. The firm analyzed public filings and alleged that RXO shifted costs of revenue to operating expenses to report 16-19% margins while industry peers made 6-8%. It also alleged that RXO changed its definition of EBITDA to avoid breaching debt covenants after cash fell to $7 million.

In a filing on January 23, 2026, RXO announced that Chief Accounting Officer Jason Kerr would retire on May 15, 2026. By February 2026, RXO had missed fourth-quarter guidance and transitioned from unsecured credit to an asset-based loan secured by $1.23 billion in accounts receivable. DF Research called the move a forced foreclosure by lenders after RXO used $566 million of its $565 million credit line.

The $1.23 billion in receivables and the $566 million in credit used are different figures: the first is money owed to RXO, and the second is debt it drew down. On May 6, 2026, DF Research noted that RXO would report first-quarter results the next day.

title: CCC sent PLN 330 million of goods to an insolvent buyer and moved to buy it
points: NINGI said that starting in November 2024, CCC sent PLN 330 million in unwanted inventory to an insolvent franchisee called MKRI, which operates Kaes and Worldbox stores.
NINGI also alleged that CCC planned to acquire MKRI from Arca REO PSA to erase the uncollectible PLN 330 million receivable through consolidation.
These two figures are separate: PLN 330 million was the inventory and receivable figure, while PLN 267.4 million was the alleged EBITDA boost.
body: CCC SA is a Polish footwear company listed in Warsaw that presented investors with a retail turnaround.

On October 16, 2025, short seller NINGI Research published a report alleging that the turnaround was an illusion. NINGI said that starting in November 2024, CCC sent PLN 330 million in unwanted inventory to an insolvent franchisee called MKRI, which operates Kaes and Worldbox stores.
The report alleged that short-term receivables rose 112% year-over-year to PLN 535 million, with PLN 130 million past due, and that the shipments inflated group EBITDA by PLN 267.4 million.

NINGI also alleged that CCC planned to acquire MKRI from Arca REO PSA to erase the uncollectible PLN 330 million receivable through consolidation. The report said that CCC's supervisory board chairman, Wieslaw Oles, secretly controlled the seller. These two figures are separate: PLN 330 million was the inventory and receivable figure, while PLN 267.4 million was the alleged EBITDA boost.

CCC denied the allegations in a rebuttal post and video conference, saying they were false and made to profit from short positions. NINGI replied the video had confirmed several findings, including that CCC was behind on its store expansion targets.

title: A small Singapore firm bought $4.8 billion of Nvidia chips. US officials opened a probe.

The Times also reported that Megaspeed spent $4.8 billion on restricted Nvidia AI chips since June 2024 and received more than 200 shipments over 12 months.
Megaspeed chief executive James Tan denied breaking US laws, saying the company's operations were legitimate and it had cooperated with investigators.
body: Megaspeed International is a Singapore-based data center and cloud computing company. It told authorities and partners that it ran a legitimate commercial cloud business outside China.

On October 9, 2025, The New York Times reported that it had visited sites in four countries, reviewed shipment records and business registrations, and interviewed more than 30 people. Megaspeed funneled Nvidia chips to data centers in Malaysia and Indonesia that appeared to remotely serve customers in China.
The Times also reported that Megaspeed spent $4.8 billion on restricted Nvidia AI chips since June 2024 and received more than 200 shipments over 12 months.

Megaspeed chief executive James Tan denied breaking US laws, saying the company's operations were legitimate and it had cooperated with investigators. Nvidia initially stated that its own compliance checks found no evidence of chip diversion.

On November 16, 2026, the US Commerce and Justice Departments announced that their investigation into potential export control violations had started in 2024 and included an in-person check in Singapore in June 2025. Singaporean police also stated that their domestic investigation into Megaspeed remained ongoing.

body: Slide Insurance Holdings is a $1.9 billion property and casualty insurer based in Tampa, Florida. Founded in 2021, the Nasdaq-listed company describes itself as a tech-enabled insurer and writes homeowners insurance policies.

On September 30, 2025, short seller Manatee Research published a report on Slide Insurance and disclosed a short position, meaning it earns when the shares fall. The report alleged that Slide's technology claims were significantly overstated.

body: Richtech Robotics is listed on Nasdaq and tells investors it designs and makes autonomous delivery robots for restaurants and hotels. The company began as Richtech Creative Displays in 2017 and became Richtech Robotics in 2022.
In August 2025, Richtech announced a Master Services Agreement with a top global retailer. Online speculation linked the deal to Walmart and fueled a sharp rise in the share price.

Capybara alleged that Richtech sold rebranded Chinese robots and relied on fake partnerships, fake deals, fabricated Walmart hype, and undisclosed related-party transactions.

body: Rezolve AI is a UK company listed on Nasdaq that sells commerce software and told investors it was an artificial intelligence company. It went public through a SPAC in late 2024 and reached a valuation of about $2 billion.

On September 29, 2025, short seller Fuzzy Panda Research published a report on the company and disclosed it held a short position, meaning it earns when the shares fall. The firm interviewed former employees, checked app store listings, and tested the company's software.

title: A $500K-a-year rare-disease drug faced claims of sham trials. The stock fell 13%.

body: Soleno Therapeutics, Inc. is a Nasdaq-listed company that sells VYKAT XR, a drug for hyperphagia and weight management in Prader-Willi syndrome. In October 2023, the company received FDA approval for the treatment.

On August 15, 2025, short seller Scorpion Capital published a report on the company and filed an FDA Citizen Petition. Scorpion Capital alleged that VYKAT XR is a $500K-a-year knockoff of a 50-year-old generic compound supported by suspect data and sham clinical trials.

The report also alleged that a physician's co-authored papers showed irregularities in data integrity and adherence to scientific standards, casting doubt on Soleno's trials, publications, and FDA submissions. Scorpion Capital suggested the drug could face market withdrawal or a drop in new prescriptions. Shares of Soleno fell 13% on the morning of August 15, 2025.
On September 25, 2025, law firm Hagens Berman issued a notice encouraging Soleno investors with losses from the August 15 drop to contact the firm.

title: A €5,080 Blazer in Moscow. Brunello Cucinelli Shares Fell 15%.

body: Brunello Cucinelli is an Italian luxury fashion company known for its cashmere clothing, valued at €7 billion. The company had told investors about its Russian business, but short seller Morpheus Research alleged that its account of those operations was misleading.

On September 25, 2025, Morpheus Research published an 84-page report based partly on visits to Moscow stores. The firm held short positions in Brunello Cucinelli shares, meaning it stood to gain if the price fell.

Its secret shopper entered a Brunello Cucinelli outlet in Moscow and documented merchandise at the GUM store on Red Square. Product tags identified the manufacturer as Brunello Cucinelli SpA and the importer as its Russian subsidiary, Brunello Cucinelli RUS OOO. At Moscow's TSUM store, investigators found a blazer priced at RUB 499,500, approximately €5,080, with a tag showing manufacture in Italy in March 2025.

Morpheus alleged that the company continued operating in Russia despite EU sanctions and engaged in aggressive discounting. On September 25, its shares fell as much as 15% when trading resumed after a suspension lasting nearly four hours.
On September 30, 2025, Bloomberg described the allegations in its coverage of the report. The article identified the central accusation as misleading investors about the company's Russian operations.

title: Aya Gold & Silver reported 100 million ounces of silver. A short seller said half was phantom.

Using satellite imagery, Blue Orca claimed the mine should have yielded 6.3 million ounces by the end of the second quarter of 2025, rather than the 3.3 million ounces mined.

body: Aya Gold & Silver Inc is a Canadian mining company listed in Toronto. It told investors its Zgounder mine in Morocco held a 100-million-ounce silver resource and would generate over $100 million in cash flows.

On September 25, 2025, Blue Orca Capital published a report and said it held a short position in the stock, earning when shares fall. The firm alleged that a 2021 resource update, produced by a business associate of CEO Benoit La Salle, inflated the silver resource by over 100%, or more than 50 million ounces.
Using satellite imagery, Blue Orca claimed the mine should have yielded 6.3 million ounces by the end of the second quarter of 2025, rather than the 3.3 million ounces mined.

Aya's shares dropped as much as 22% before closing down 2.6% that day, and later rebounded. The company denied the allegations, calling them inaccurate and aimed at profiting from a share drop. The share price fall and the alleged missing silver are separate figures: the first reflects market trading, while the second is an unverified claim about ore in the ground.

On December 2, 2025, Blue Orca issued an update noting that Aya's third-quarter open-pit grades fell to 123 grams per tonne and that the miner attributed lower grades to intentionally leaving high-grade ore in the ground.

title: goeasy Reported 9% Loan Losses. A Short Seller Calculated 15%.
points: Jehoshaphat alleged that goeasy had delayed approximately $300 million in loan charge-offs.
The report estimated that the actual net charge-off rate should have been closer to 15%, rather than 9%.
The report also alleged that goeasy had moved about 8% of its loan book into a lower-risk category without an apparent change in credit scores.
body: goeasy Ltd. is a Canadian lender that makes loans to borrowers with weaker credit. It reported a net charge-off rate of 9%, a measure of loans it expected not to recover. Its reported delinquency rates had also improved.

On September 22, 2025, Jehoshaphat Research published a report after months of studying goeasy's accounting and comparing annual reports. The firm held a short position, meaning it stood to gain if goeasy's shares fell.

Jehoshaphat alleged that goeasy had delayed approximately $300 million in loan charge-offs. It attributed roughly $100 million to a changed policy for writing off overdue loans and roughly $200 million to how the company classified delinquencies. The report estimated that the actual net charge-off rate should have been closer to 15%, rather than 9%.

The report also alleged that goeasy had moved about 8% of its loan book into a lower-risk category without an apparent change in credit scores. It pointed to growing unpaid interest receivable as another sign that borrowers were struggling to repay.

goeasy shares fell 3% on September 22, 2025, following the report. Jehoshaphat's research archive also carried a headline describing a 60% share decline linked to an accounting restatement and higher loan losses, without giving a date or further details.

title: A soccer holding company pivoted to a $300 million crypto treasury
points: The report said Brera's Italian sports clubs, including Brera Milano, Juve Stabia, and UYBA Volley, generated minimal revenue and served mainly for publicity.
Fugazi Research alleged that Brera shifted toward capital-markets engineering.

body: Brera Holdings PLC is an Ireland-based holding company that listed on Nasdaq in January 2023. It promoted a plan to own multiple social-impact soccer clubs.

body: Marex Group Plc is a UK broker listed on Nasdaq. It reported profits and strong operating cash flow, while short seller NINGI Research alleged its accounts overstated both.
