body: Flux Power Holdings is a US manufacturer of lithium-ion battery systems for forklifts and airport ground support equipment. It buys battery cells from China, assembles them into packs, and sells them to equipment makers.

On July 23, 2025, Sunshine Research published a report saying Flux Power was an attractive short. It noted that on February 3, 2025, Flux Power had disclosed falling below the Nasdaq minimum of $2.5 million in stockholder equity, with a compliance extension expiring on July 30, 2025.

Sunshine Research wrote that Flux Power had reported a negative book value of $4.3 million on March 31, 2025, leaving a $6.8 million gap. To cover 4 to 8 quarters of ongoing operating losses, the investigator estimated the company needed to raise $14.6 million to $22.3 million, equal to 30% to 65% of its market cap.

On July 23, 2025, the shares dipped to $1.97 intraday and closed at $2.12. By the end of that week, the share price had fallen 11%, from $2.06 to $1.83, as investors weighed the compliance deadline and possible dilution.

title: Aether listed on Nasdaq with $3,000 in equipment and a 235-square-foot virtual office
points: BMF Reports said Aether's filings claimed no material relationship with 28 Ventures and omitted that FINRA had permanently barred Cid in January 2022.
The report also said Aether had only a $12K-a-year virtual office of 235 square feet and less than $3,000 in net property and equipment.
Shareholder law firms Robbins LLP and Johnson Fistel announced investigations into Aether in June and October 2026 over possible securities law violations.
body: Aether Holdings, Inc. operates a financial technology platform in the United States. It listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market in April 2025, raising about $8.901 million in its initial public offering.

On July 23, 2025, short seller BMF Reports published a report on Aether. It alleged that Chief Executive Officer Nicolas Lin and business development head Frank Cid used a shell entity, 28 Ventures Aether, to sell 428,572 shares right after the offering despite a lock-up clause.

BMF Reports said Aether's filings claimed no material relationship with 28 Ventures and omitted that FINRA had permanently barred Cid in January 2022. The report also said Aether had only a $12K-a-year virtual office of 235 square feet and less than $3,000 in net property and equipment.
Shareholder law firms Robbins LLP and Johnson Fistel announced investigations into Aether in June and October 2026 over possible securities law violations.

title: Enovis Claimed 6-10% Organic Growth. A Short Seller Calculated 2%.
points: Jehoshaphat held a short position, which meant it stood to profit if Enovis shares fell.
Against the company's stated 6-10%, Jehoshaphat arrived at 2%.
It said Enovis had generated negative free cash flow in aggregate for 20 years under different owners and managers.
body: Enovis Corporation is a US medical technology company focused on orthopedic products. It told investors that sales from its existing business grew organically by 6-10%, meaning growth apart from acquisitions. Analysts had seen the company meet quarterly earnings estimates for ten years.

On July 17, 2025, Jehoshaphat Research published a report alleging that Enovis had inflated its organic revenue growth and profits for years. Jehoshaphat held a short position, which meant it stood to profit if Enovis shares fell.

The investigator said it examined irregularities in Enovis's reported figures and recalculated organic growth by hand. Against the company's stated 6-10%, Jehoshaphat arrived at 2%. The report argued that repeated acquisitions had helped support the company's reported performance while debt had reached a level that would restrict further deals.

Jehoshaphat also challenged Enovis's adjusted EBITDA and predicted that the company would continue generating negative free cash flow. It said Enovis had generated negative free cash flow in aggregate for 20 years under different owners and managers.
The CEO who had overseen Enovis's acquisition program had resigned the previous quarter. That resignation preceded the short seller's report.

title: UnitedHealth gave $9 billion in cyberattack loans, then sued over repayment
points: In May, July, and January 2026, The New York Times and The Guardian reported on probes and lawsuits facing the company.
A ransomware attack on its Change Healthcare unit exposed the data of 190 million people, and Change gave $9 billion in interest-free loans to more than 10,000 medical providers.
UnitedHealth called the plaintiffs' motions a collective shakedown and asked a court to reject an injunction against loan repayment.
body: UnitedHealth Group is a US health care company with $400 billion in revenue that insures 50 million people and employs 135,000 doctors and clinicians. It told investors its scale lets it coordinate care and earn steady profits, and said medical decisions are made only by patients and doctors.

In May, July, and January 2026, The New York Times and The Guardian reported on probes and lawsuits facing the company. A ransomware attack on its Change Healthcare unit exposed the data of 190 million people, and Change gave $9 billion in interest-free loans to more than 10,000 medical providers.

Two Minnesota medical practices alleged in court filings that UnitedHealthcare denied late claims while pressuring them to repay loans, of which about $5.5 billion had been repaid a year later. UnitedHealth called the plaintiffs' motions a collective shakedown and asked a court to reject an injunction against loan repayment.

On July 24, 2025, UnitedHealth said it was cooperating with a Justice Department probe into its Medicare billing practices. On January 7, 2026, US senators Ron Wyden and Elizabeth Warren wrote that UnitedHealth had declined to produce internal records on bonuses paid to nursing homes that reduce hospital transfers.

title: Vedanta valued its Zambian copper assets at $2.7 billion. A liquidator reported $1.1 billion.
points: Viceroy later alleged that ₹3,247 crore in brand fees went to Vedanta Resources without clear services in return.
On August 29, Viceroy reported findings from staff interviews, site inspections, drone footage, satellite images and financial analysis.
Viceroy reported that an April 14 explosion at Vedanta's Chhattisgarh Athena Power Plant had killed at least 20 workers and injured over 36.
body: Vedanta Limited is an Indian mining and energy company. Its parent, Vedanta Resources Limited, repeatedly promised creditors that it would separate businesses and reduce debt.

On July 30, 2025, Viceroy Research alleged that Vedanta Resources and the Agarwal family were extracting money from Vedanta Limited. The short-selling research firm cited whistleblowers and reported that India's Enforcement Directorate had summoned Vedanta Limited's CEO and CFO in July 2023 over improper brand fee payments.

Viceroy later alleged that ₹3,247 crore in brand fees went to Vedanta Resources without clear services in return. On August 29, Viceroy reported findings from staff interviews, site inspections, drone footage, satellite images and financial analysis. Vedanta valued Konkola Copper Mines' property, plant and equipment at $2.7 billion, while its liquidator had reported $1.1 billion the previous year.

On September 17, 2025, Viceroy challenged Vedanta's proposed JAL acquisition. It reported a 6% EBITDA margin, negative operating earnings and a -29% net margin for JAL in FY25. Viceroy warned that financing the acquisition with new debt would weaken liquidity.

On April 16, 2026, Viceroy reported that an April 14 explosion at Vedanta's Chhattisgarh Athena Power Plant had killed at least 20 workers and injured over 36. Vedanta said the incident involved subcontractor NGSL personnel.

title: Hindustan Zinc shares fell 4.8% as Viceroy alleged cash was drained
points: On July 9, Hindustan Zinc shares fell 4.8% to Rs 415.30, while Vedanta Limited shares fell as much as 7.7% to Rs 421.
On August 25, it reported that Hindustan Zinc had paid ₹1,060 crore ($121m) in Brand and Strategic Services fees to Vedanta Limited in Q1 FY26, which was then remitted to Vedanta Resources.
It said the payment represented a 61% increase over the previous year.
body: Hindustan Zinc is a subsidiary of Vedanta Limited, part of the Vedanta group. On July 9, 2025, short-seller Viceroy Research challenged the group's finances and alleged that its parent company depended on cash extracted from operating businesses.

Viceroy alleged that Vedanta Resources Limited took cash from Vedanta Limited to service its own debt, forcing the operating company to borrow more. The report described the group structure as financially unsustainable and alleged material discrepancies in its finances.

On July 9, Hindustan Zinc shares fell 4.8% to Rs 415.30, while Vedanta Limited shares fell as much as 7.7% to Rs 421. These were share-price movements, not amounts of cash allegedly transferred. Viceroy disclosed that its financial interests could benefit from falling security prices.

Viceroy continued publishing allegations about Hindustan Zinc. On August 25, it reported that Hindustan Zinc had paid ₹1,060 crore ($121m) in Brand and Strategic Services fees to Vedanta Limited in Q1 FY26, which was then remitted to Vedanta Resources. It said the payment represented a 61% increase over the previous year.

On October 23, Viceroy reported that Vedanta Resources had disclosed in its September 30, 2025 bond prospectus that the group had received summons from SEBI based on Viceroy's research. The disclosure established that the securities regulator had issued summons, not that Viceroy's allegations had been proven.

title: Bitmine Immersion raised $250 million to buy Ethereum while holding zero tokens
points: Fugazi Research alleged that Bitmine held zero Ethereum tokens while its stock soared over 2,500% to $160 per share on a float of 3.2 million shares.
The report said the 55 million insider shares included full resale rights and noted that the chief executive's private company owned the mining rigs and took 88% of the Bitcoin produced.
Kerrisdale also alleged that a $365 million direct offering promoted as accretive at $70 per share was actually a discount once attached warrants were counted.
body: Bitmine Immersion Technologies is a Las Vegas-based digital-asset company that previously mined Bitcoin and told investors it was becoming a large Ethereum treasury vehicle. On June 30, 2025, the company announced a $250 million private placement of 55 million shares at $4.50 each to fund Ethereum purchases.

On July 9, 2025, Fugazi Research alleged that Bitmine held zero Ethereum tokens while its stock soared over 2,500% to $160 per share on a float of 3.2 million shares. The report said the 55 million insider shares included full resale rights and noted that the chief executive's private company owned the mining rigs and took 88% of the Bitcoin produced.

On October 8, 2025, Kerrisdale Capital published a report and said it held a short position, earning if the stock fell. Kerrisdale alleged that Bitmine had issued more than $10 billion in new stock over three months, or about $170 million per day, to accumulate over 2.8 million tokens while stopping weekly share-count updates.

Kerrisdale also alleged that a $365 million direct offering promoted as accretive at $70 per share was actually a discount once attached warrants were counted. Bitmine shares fell 2% on October 8, 2025.

On March 5, 2026, Culper Research wrote that Bitmine, led by chairman Tom Lee, was overwhelmingly responsible for driving Ethereum staking demand, with the staking entry queue sitting at 3.35 million tokens.

title: 86 servers and 588 subscription sellers leaked fleet data through Uffizio software
points: The investigator stated that Uffizio software and its deployment by hundreds of global resellers leaked sensitive fleet data across at least 12 countries for over five years.
The investigator found 86 IP addresses with JSON files and 588 subscription selling companies selling Uffizio products under their own brand.
The investigator noted that a CISA Advisory was published on October 18, 2021, affecting equipment referred to as Uffizio GPS Tracker, vulnerable to five vulnerabilities.
body: Uffizio is a software company in India that provides a GPS tracking software service supporting over 1,200 trackers and managing data sent by GPS trackers produced by various manufacturers. The company told investors and the public that it was GDPR compliant.

On July 7, 2025, Deep Specter Research published a report stating that it uncovered a multi-year data exposure involving Uffizio. The investigator stated that Uffizio software and its deployment by hundreds of global resellers leaked sensitive fleet data across at least 12 countries for over five years.

The report said that the exposure continued even after a public CVE disclosure and an internal GDPR audit. The investigator found 86 IP addresses with JSON files and 588 subscription selling companies selling Uffizio products under their own brand.

The investigator noted that a CISA Advisory was published on October 18, 2021, affecting equipment referred to as Uffizio GPS Tracker, vulnerable to five vulnerabilities. The report also stated that an internal GDPR audit by Uffizio was completed on June 30, 2021, and that leaks continued until 2022, with some servers managed by Uffizio resuming leaks in 2023.

title: TMC projected $6.8 billion in value. Iceberg calculated negative $721 million.
points: TMC had estimated third-party processing costs of $76 per wet tonne.
Iceberg said supplier PAMCO's website indicated $120 per wet tonne, 57% more.
Iceberg subsequently reported that the investment totaled $85 million.
body: TMC is a Nasdaq-listed deep-sea mining company that plans to collect metal-bearing nodules from the seabed. It projected a net present value of $6.8 billion for its mining project and said in November 2024 that its pre-feasibility study was complete.

On May 27, 2025, Iceberg Research challenged those projections. It reviewed TMC's financial assumptions, supplier costs and pilot-test data, then estimated a negative net present value of $721 million, compared with TMC's positive $6.8 billion projection.

TMC had estimated third-party processing costs of $76 per wet tonne. Iceberg said supplier PAMCO's website indicated $120 per wet tonne, 57% more. It also challenged TMC's assumed nickel recovery rate of 95%, citing 83% at comparable projects.
On June 16, TMC announced an investment by Korea Zinc. Its shares rose from $4.63 to $6.75 on the news. Iceberg subsequently reported that the investment totaled $85 million.

On August 18, 2025, Iceberg examined TMC's newly released pre-feasibility study. It reported that projected offshore costs had increased 152%, from $56 to $141 per wet tonne, while the study retained a 95% nickel recovery assumption. Iceberg also challenged the study's metal prices and zero US royalty assumption.

title: Eutelsat carried 3 billion euros in net debt. A short seller saw a 70% drop.
points: HitHawk presented a short case for the stock, meaning it would earn money if the shares fell.
The report also raised concerns about the company's 3 billion euros of net debt.
HitHawk issued a price target that implied about 70% downside for the shares.
body: Eutelsat Communications is a European satellite company listed in Paris under the ticker ETL. Its shares had recently rallied on expectations around a new chief executive and a capital injection from France.
On July 6, 2025, HitHawk Research published a report on the company. HitHawk presented a short case for the stock, meaning it would earn money if the shares fell.

HitHawk alleged that Eutelsat lagged far behind competitors such as Starlink and Kuiper in technology, scale, and innovation. The report also raised concerns about the company's 3 billion euros of net debt.

HitHawk issued a price target that implied about 70% downside for the shares. The debt and the price target are different types of figures - one is money the company owed, and the other is an estimate of where the stock could trade.

title: Carrefour reported €8.8 billion in net debt. An activist fund said it was €10.4 billion.
points: Whitelight Capital held an undisclosed stake in Carrefour, and shares rose 0.27% to 13.3 euros that day.
Whitelight Capital founder Kevin Romanteau alleged that Carrefour used accounting maneuvers to hide at least €1.5 billion in debt.
He said net debt was actually €10.4 billion rather than €8.8 billion and threatened legal action against board members.
body: Carrefour is a French supermarket group led by CEO Alexandre Bompard. It reported €8.8 billion in net debt.

On March 10, 2025, France-based activist fund Whitelight Capital warned that rising tensions with Carrefour franchise stores in France created structural risks for shareholders. The Carrefour Franchisees Association, which represents 260 stores, had launched an alternative purchasing network named Project X and had previously sued Carrefour over product prices. Whitelight Capital held an undisclosed stake in Carrefour, and shares rose 0.27% to 13.3 euros that day.

On July 4, 2025, Whitelight Capital founder Kevin Romanteau alleged that Carrefour used accounting maneuvers to hide at least €1.5 billion in debt. He said net debt was actually €10.4 billion rather than €8.8 billion and threatened legal action against board members. Romanteau also suggested that delisting Carrefour's Brazilian branch could allow the operations to continue more discreetly.
An internal source at Carrefour rejected the accusation. The source pointed to the company's BBB rating from Standard & Poor's and said factoring was a well-known practice disclosed in the accounts.

title: BCG modelled relocating Palestinians from Gaza under a multimillion-dollar contract

body: Boston Consulting Group is a consulting firm.

On July 4, 2025, the Financial Times reported that Boston Consulting Group had modelled the costs of relocating Palestinians from Gaza. The newspaper also reported that the firm entered into a multimillion-dollar contract to help launch an aid scheme for Gaza and advised the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation and Safe Reach Solutions on their operations there.
Chief executive Christoph Schweizer stated that the Gaza work was disavowed and partners exited the firm.

On July 24, 2025, Boston Consulting Group announced the results of an investigation it had commissioned. The firm said some of its U.S.-based staff had sidestepped its risk controls to do work related to the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation and post-war reconstruction for Gaza.

title: Nutex Took a $55 Million Charge for Arbitration Claims It Could Not Collect
points: On November 26, Nutex challenged the short seller's credibility, saying Capybara Research appeared not to exist as an identifiable entity.
On December 16, Capybara published a second report alleging that former employees had described pressure from Vo to improperly code medical bills and overcharge insurers.
Capybara said Nutex had taken a $55 million charge for arbitration claims the company determined were ineligible for reimbursement.
body: Nutex Health is a Houston-based healthcare company that operates emergency rooms and small hospitals. It reported third-quarter revenue of $268 million and adjusted EBITDA of $105 million. The company operated 24 facilities across 11 states.

On November 25, 2025, Capybara Research published an investigation based on interviews with former insiders and business partners. It alleged that founder and CEO Thomas Vo had engaged in fraud, embezzlement and self-dealing. Capybara said Nutex had been removed from more than a dozen emergency rooms.

On November 26, Nutex challenged the short seller's credibility, saying Capybara Research appeared not to exist as an identifiable entity. On December 16, Capybara published a second report alleging that former employees had described pressure from Vo to improperly code medical bills and overcharge insurers.

On October 15, 2026, Capybara said Nutex had taken a $55 million charge for arbitration claims the company determined were ineligible for reimbursement. Capybara had previously alleged that such claims inflated receivables. The charge concerned amounts Nutex could not collect, not money stolen. Capybara, which disclosed a short position, said the shares fell over 20% on the news. Its affiliates stood to profit from a falling share price.

body: Kinsale Capital Group is a specialty property-and-casualty insurer listed on the New York Stock Exchange. It sells coverage for unusual or hard-to-place risks, and its stock rose about 1,560% after its July 2016 initial public offering.

In July 2025, short seller PAA Research published a report setting a $230 price objective on the shares. It later reported that gross premiums written declined 3.5% year-over-year compared to the same period in 2025.

On May 7, 2026, Edwin Dorsey published a report on The Bear Cave. He filed public record requests and obtained customer complaints sent to insurance regulators alleging overcharges, improper billing, and ineffective coverage.

The Bear Cave alleged that Kinsale relied on overpriced, exclusion-heavy policies and minimal regulatory oversight rather than superior underwriting. By May 24, 2026, one commentator noted the share price had fallen 35% since PAA Research's July 2025 publication.

title: INmune Bio issued 600,000 shares to a consultant using a virtual shell office
points: The report said INmune Bio built its valuation on an abandoned drug and selective quotes from unblinded observations rather than sound science.
BMF Reports also alleged that INmune Bio paid 600,000 restricted shares priced at $2.50 to a consulting entity using a virtual shell office in Vancouver, Canada, and a fake LinkedIn identity.
INmune Bio had reported a $42.1 million net loss in 2024, up from $30 million the previous year.
body: INmune Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company listed on Nasdaq. It told investors its lead drug candidate, XPro1595, could treat neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease.

On June 27, 2025, short seller BMF Reports published an investigation into the company's trial design and filings. The report said INmune Bio built its valuation on an abandoned drug and selective quotes from unblinded observations rather than sound science.

BMF Reports also alleged that INmune Bio paid 600,000 restricted shares priced at $2.50 to a consulting entity using a virtual shell office in Vancouver, Canada, and a fake LinkedIn identity. It added that SEC filings showed repeated stock, option, and cash payments to consulting entities that appeared to vanish outside of Edgar.
INmune Bio had reported a $42.1 million net loss in 2024, up from $30 million the previous year.

title: Lennar beat its delivery forecast by 340 homes after its spinoff bought 356
points: By checking county records and Zillow listings, Hunterbrook identified more than 700 Millrose purchases across 15 states, worth an estimated $200 million or more in about a month.
Hunterbrook estimated the rented homes would return about 5% a year before interest, below Millrose's 6.5% to 6.75% bond rates.
Hunterbrook reported that reporters visited 36 Millrose houses in Florida and 39 in Texas and found more than 95% of analyzed purchases advertised for rent.
body: Lennar is America's second-largest homebuilder. In 2025, it spun off Millrose Properties to hold land for future construction, with Lennar CEO Stuart Miller as Millrose's largest voting shareholder. Lennar told investors that weak numbers came from soft demand and deliberate price cuts.

On October 2, 2026, Hunterbrook Media reported that Millrose had changed its agreements in August to buy Lennar's finished homes, while affiliate Hunterbrook Capital held short positions in both stocks. By checking county records and Zillow listings, Hunterbrook identified more than 700 Millrose purchases across 15 states, worth an estimated $200 million or more in about a month.

The report said at least 356 of those purchases closed in the final week of Lennar's third fiscal quarter, helping Lennar beat its delivery forecast by 340 homes. Hunterbrook estimated the rented homes would return about 5% a year before interest, below Millrose's 6.5% to 6.75% bond rates.

Millrose told Goldman Sachs it bought homes with signed leases already in place. On October 8, 2026, Hunterbrook reported that reporters visited 36 Millrose houses in Florida and 39 in Texas and found more than 95% of analyzed purchases advertised for rent.

title: D.R. Horton faced 198 South Carolina court complaints over 10 years
points: It found 198 complaints filed against D.R.
Horton in South Carolina county courts over 10 years, and noted that contracts required private arbitration.
A law firm told Hunterbrook that about 500 South Carolina homeowners had contacted it with complaints, with 125 cases under investigation.
body: D.R. Horton is the largest homebuilder in the United States. The company remained profitable even as its stock price fell more than 30% in the previous year amid cooling demand and rising costs.

Hunterbrook Media interviewed homeowners, former employees, and building experts, and reviewed purchase agreements, warranty policies, and court records. Its investment affiliate, Hunterbrook Capital, held no position in the company at publication.

Hunterbrook alleged that the builder cut corners, discouraged third-party inspections, and pushed repair costs onto buyers. It found 198 complaints filed against D.R. Horton in South Carolina county courts over 10 years, and noted that contracts required private arbitration.

On June 26, 2025, Hunterbrook published its report and said it was working with litigators on potential lawsuits. A law firm told Hunterbrook that about 500 South Carolina homeowners had contacted it with complaints, with 125 cases under investigation.

title: Worldline handled 500 billion euros a year. Reporters found 580 high-fee merchants.
points: Mediapart and 20 other media outlets in the European Investigative Collaborations network examined confidential Worldline documents.
According to the report, more than 580 e-merchants paid over 5% in commission.
Worldline shares fell more than a third after the June 2025 report.
body: Worldline is a French payment processor that handles 500 billion euros in card transactions each year. The company told investors it had strengthened merchant risk controls and ended non-compliant client ties since 2023.

In June 2025, Mediapart and 20 other media outlets in the European Investigative Collaborations network examined confidential Worldline documents. The outlets alleged that Worldline processed billions of euros in fraudulent payments for online scammers and illegal casinos over ten years.

According to the report, more than 580 e-merchants paid over 5% in commission. The outlets also stated that after German regulator BaFin banned Worldline unit Payone from working with 450 clients in 2023, Worldline kept serving hundreds of them through other units.
Worldline shares fell more than a third after the June 2025 report. The company stated it would cooperate with authorities.

Fewer than three days after the initial publication, Belgian prosecutors opened a money laundering investigation into Worldline's Belgian unit. On November 6, 2025, Mediapart reported that Payone was named in German court proceedings involving online fraud networks.

title: Microvast reported up to 250 staff at a German plant. Investigators found fewer than 30 cars.
points: It said 39 of 41 random checks at the German plant showed almost no truck traffic and fewer than 30 cars on average in the parking lot.
It also alleged the China factory employed about 1,400 people and that more than 95% of non-Chinese clients were tiny startups.
Microvast had previously been denied a $200 million U.S. government grant over suspected Chinese government ties, which management denied.
body: Microvast Holdings is a Texas-based battery maker listed on Nasdaq. It told investors it had hundreds of millions in revenue, up to 250 workers at a plant near Berlin and over 2,500 at a factory in China.

On June 25, 2025, short seller Grizzly Research published a report after visiting the sites and checking satellite images. It said 39 of 41 random checks at the German plant showed almost no truck traffic and fewer than 30 cars on average in the parking lot. It also alleged the China factory employed about 1,400 people and that more than 95% of non-Chinese clients were tiny startups.

Grizzly Research further alleged that the Chinese government held a stake in Microvast's main Chinese unit. Microvast had previously been denied a $200 million U.S. government grant over suspected Chinese government ties, which management denied.

Microvast shares fell 7% that Wednesday, dropping as much as $0.40, or 10.23%, during trading before closing at $3.90. On August 1, 2025, Microvast announced that Chief Financial Officer Charles Schultz was leaving after three months. On September 2, 2026, a law firm announced a shareholder class action lawsuit covering shares bought through March 16, 2026.

title: CTO Realty Growth had a $38 million dividend shortfall and raised share count by 70%
points: The report alleged that CTO excluded recurring capital expenditures from its Adjusted Funds From Operation metric, which also determined 70% of management's performance pay.
Wolfpack alleged that CTO had a $38 million dividend shortfall from 2021 to 2024 and increased its shares outstanding by 70% since December 2022 to cover it.
The report further alleged that CTO did not impair a loan after a tenant stopped paying rent in November 2022 and an affiliate and its owner filed for bankruptcy in early 2023.
body: CTO Realty Growth is a real estate investment trust listed on the New York Stock Exchange that buys and manages shopping centers. It told investors about its dividend sustainability and used an Adjusted Funds From Operation metric.

On June 25, 2025, short seller Wolfpack Research published a report analyzing the company and its proxy filings, and said it held a short position in the stock. The report alleged that CTO excluded recurring capital expenditures from its Adjusted Funds From Operation metric, which also determined 70% of management's performance pay.

Wolfpack alleged that CTO had a $38 million dividend shortfall from 2021 to 2024 and increased its shares outstanding by 70% since December 2022 to cover it. The report also alleged CTO held $8.4 million in cash against $14 million in quarterly dividends, $5.7 million in average quarterly recurring capital expenditures, and about $12 million in additional planned capital expenditures.

The report further alleged that CTO did not impair a loan after a tenant stopped paying rent in November 2022 and an affiliate and its owner filed for bankruptcy in early 2023. CTO shares fell 3.7% on June 25, 2025.

title: A short activist pointed to a 1936 seizure at perfume retailer Douglas AG
points: HitHawk described Douglas AG as a legacy retailer in decline with unsustainable debt, reliance on shrinking high-street traffic and a weak digital presence.
HitHawk also alleged that the perfumery that became Douglas was likely seized from Jewish owners in 1936 and handed to a Nazi-approved businessman.
The report said the company faces potential legal claims for restitution and reputational damage.
body: Douglas AG is a large German perfume and beauty retailer listed in Frankfurt under the ticker DOU with a market value of EUR1.17 billion. Its shares had fallen about 50% since its March 2024 initial public offering.

On June 15, 2025, Europe-focused short activist HitHawk Research published a report on the company. HitHawk described Douglas AG as a legacy retailer in decline with unsustainable debt, reliance on shrinking high-street traffic and a weak digital presence.

HitHawk also alleged that the perfumery that became Douglas was likely seized from Jewish owners in 1936 and handed to a Nazi-approved businessman. The report said the company faces potential legal claims for restitution and reputational damage.

title: The RealReal sold used luxury goods. Its checks allegedly let fakes through.
points: The firm alleged that The RealReal's authentication process let through many counterfeit products.
It said the problem had angered both buyers and sellers and damaged their trust in the company.
The researchers said they found no evidence that the technology was effective.
body: The RealReal is a Nasdaq-listed company that sells used luxury goods. Its business depends on checking whether those goods are genuine before selling them to buyers. Customers rely on those checks when deciding whether to buy.

On June 11, 2025, J Capital Research published a short report questioning those checks. The firm alleged that The RealReal's authentication process let through many counterfeit products. It said the problem had angered both buyers and sellers and damaged their trust in the company.

J Capital also examined the company's use of artificial intelligence to speed up authentication. The researchers said they found no evidence that the technology was effective. They argued that The RealReal handled too many different kinds of products for its authenticators to receive adequate training.

The report questioned whether the business could operate profitably while keeping counterfeit goods out. J Capital argued that processing enough products to become profitable would inevitably allow fakes through. The allegation concerned the reliability of authentication, not a stated amount of financial loss.
The report appeared on June 11, 2025. J Capital's published assessment was that The RealReal's business model might not work because of the difficulty of authenticating goods at scale.

title: Yorkville sought $150 million for a SPAC after years of regulatory fines
points: Shortfinder also listed past regulatory actions against Yorkville Advisors.

In 2011, Italian regulators fined Yorkville and its chairman for breaking takeover rules, and in 2012, the SEC sued Yorkville over allegations that it reported false and inflated values for certain securities.
Yorkville settled a Swiss investigation into alleged reporting failures on derivative holdings in three Swiss-listed companies.
body: Yorkville Acquisition Corp. is a blank-check company sponsored by Yorkville Advisors Global, LP. It filed an amended prospectus to raise $150 million in an initial public offering at $10.00 per unit.

On June 10, 2025, short-selling research platform Shortfinder published a report on the offering. Shortfinder said Yorkville Advisors manages offshore hedge funds that buy discounted stock, warrants, and convertible debt from small companies and sell the shares into public markets, which often pushes down stock prices.

Shortfinder also listed past regulatory actions against Yorkville Advisors. In 2011, Italian regulators fined Yorkville and its chairman for breaking takeover rules, and in 2012, the SEC sued Yorkville over allegations that it reported false and inflated values for certain securities.

In May 2022, Yorkville settled a Swiss investigation into alleged reporting failures on derivative holdings in three Swiss-listed companies. The Tax Court also sided with the IRS in a separate dispute, which Yorkville is appealing.

title: Shortfinder published 50 reports and commented on Trump Media's financier
points: It designs research for short sellers and risk-aware investors focusing on small- and micro-cap equities, and it has published 50 reports since 2025.
In an article published on July 21, 2026, CapitalScope founder Justin Hibbard commented on companies linked to such financing.
He said they are often companies that cannot get traditional financing or a traditional IPO.
body: Trump Media & Technology Group Corp. is a United States company and the home of Truth Social. Angelo's Yorkville Advisors, a small New Jersey investment firm, was a large stakeholder in the company.

Shortfinder is a Los Angeles paid research platform run by equity-research firm CapitalScope. It designs research for short sellers and risk-aware investors focusing on small- and micro-cap equities, and it has published 50 reports since 2025.

In an article published on July 21, 2026, CapitalScope founder Justin Hibbard commented on companies linked to such financing. He said they are often companies that cannot get traditional financing or a traditional IPO.
The news report also noted Trump Media's pivot into nuclear energy involving Yorkville Advisors. On June 10, 2025, Shortfinder was listed as having exposed the case.

title: Groupon touted $40.6 million in free cash flow before a short seller questioned its books
points: The report accused Groupon of using dubious accounting methods and misleading investors about the success of its turnaround strategies.
Groupon shares dropped $1.61, or nearly 5%, that day to close at $31.33.
Law firm Pomerantz LLP announced an investigation into Groupon's business practices and the securities fraud claims raised by the report.
body: Groupon is a two-sided marketplace where consumers buy local deals and vouchers from merchants. In March 2025, the company told investors its turnaround was working, pointing to $40.6 million in positive free cash flow and 8% year-over-year growth in North America Local billings.

On June 9, 2025, short seller The Captain's Log published a report questioning those claims. The report accused Groupon of using dubious accounting methods and misleading investors about the success of its turnaround strategies.
Groupon shares dropped $1.61, or nearly 5%, that day to close at $31.33. The drop in share price reflects lost market value rather than cash taken from the company.
On June 22, 2025, law firm Pomerantz LLP announced an investigation into Groupon's business practices and the securities fraud claims raised by the report.

title: SharpLink announced a $425 million Ethereum pivot. SEC filings showed no holdings.
points: The report also noted a 1-for-12 reverse stock split on May 1, 2025, that cut the public float below 700,000 shares before a 4.5 million share offering on May 20, 2025.
The share price rose 4,000% during the Ethereum pivot and then fell 90.01% following the report.
Fugazi Research reported that SharpLink's float had expanded to over 70 million shares after insiders sold.
body: SharpLink Gaming is a Nasdaq-listed digital marketing firm that converts sports fans into bettors. In 2025, it announced a $425 million private placement led by ConsenSys to stockpile Ethereum.
On June 6, 2025, short seller Fugazi Research published a report on the company. Its affiliates or clients may hold short positions in the shares, earning money when the stock falls.

Fugazi Research checked SEC filings and blockchain records and said it found no Ethereum holdings or public wallet addresses tied to SharpLink. The report also noted a 1-for-12 reverse stock split on May 1, 2025, that cut the public float below 700,000 shares before a 4.5 million share offering on May 20, 2025.

The share price rose 4,000% during the Ethereum pivot and then fell 90.01% following the report. By July 9, 2025, Fugazi Research reported that SharpLink's float had expanded to over 70 million shares after insiders sold.

title: 146 million Newsmax shares were registered for resale while cash stood at $15.1 million.
points: The report noted that Newsmax would receive none of the proceeds from those resales and had a cash burn rate of $2.8 million per month, leaving a runway of five to six months.
Exercising warrants would bring $13.3 million in cash while adding 6.9 million new shares to the market.
Newsmax shares fell 10% to close at $16.19 the day before the report, after dropping from nearly $20.00 earlier that week.
body: Newsmax, Inc. is a US public company that went public in April 2025. It reported a net loss of $8.4 million in the first quarter and held $15.1 million in cash as of March 31, 2025.

On June 6, 2025, research platform Shortfinder published a report examining SEC filings for Newsmax stock. Shortfinder pointed to two resale prospectuses declared effective by the SEC: one for 121.2 million shares held by more than 8,000 pre-IPO insiders, and another for up to 25.6 million Class B shares held by hedge fund YA II PN, Ltd.

The report noted that Newsmax would receive none of the proceeds from those resales and had a cash burn rate of $2.8 million per month, leaving a runway of five to six months. Exercising warrants would bring $13.3 million in cash while adding 6.9 million new shares to the market.
Newsmax shares fell 10% to close at $16.19 the day before the report, after dropping from nearly $20.00 earlier that week.

title: 61% of Abacus revenue came from gains on policies it still held
points: Morpheus Research published a 76-page report prepared over three months, with more than 400 citations and interviews with industry experts and former employees.
After adopting fair value accounting on June 30, 2023, Abacus reported $53.8 million in unrealized gains in 2024, representing 48% of revenue.
It said an outside actuarial firm, Lewis and Ellis, reviewed more than 700 policies without using Lapetus estimates.
body: Abacus Global Management is a US asset manager that buys and sells life insurance policies. It promoted returns of around 30% with little risk and described a potential market worth $233 billion.

On June 4, 2025, Morpheus Research published a 76-page report prepared over three months, with more than 400 citations and interviews with industry experts and former employees. Morpheus held a short position in Abacus shares, meaning it stood to profit if the price fell.

The report alleged that Abacus inflated revenue by raising the recorded value of policies it still owned. After adopting fair value accounting on June 30, 2023, Abacus reported $53.8 million in unrealized gains in 2024, representing 48% of revenue. By Q1 2025, such gains accounted for 61%. These were accounting gains, not cash received.

Morpheus questioned life expectancy estimates supplied by Lapetus Solutions, which affected policy valuations. Abacus rejected the report and threatened legal action. It said an outside actuarial firm, Lewis and Ellis, reviewed more than 700 policies without using Lapetus estimates.

On June 12, 2025, Morpheus published a follow-up disputing Abacus's response. It alleged undisclosed dealings with National Insurance Brokerage, an entity controlled by Abacus management, and challenged the company's explanation of its valuation methods.

title: A 49-slide presentation questioned Yalla Group's revenue and downloads
points: Short seller Pelican Way Research published a 49-slide presentation on the company.
Pelican Way compared Yalla's reported revenue metrics and downloads against third-party sources and its own calculations.
Two other firms, Akram's Razor and Swan Street Research, had previously alleged similar inflated user metrics against Yalla in May 2021.
body: Yalla Group is an audio-based social network listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker YALA. The company operates voice and live-room products in Gulf markets and the Middle East.

On June 2, 2025, short seller Pelican Way Research published a 49-slide presentation on the company. Pelican Way compared Yalla's reported revenue metrics and downloads against third-party sources and its own calculations.
The presentation alleged that Yalla's reported figures sharply contrasted with those sources. Pelican Way also alleged that the company's app reviews showed signs of extreme artificial activity.
Two other firms, Akram's Razor and Swan Street Research, had previously alleged similar inflated user metrics against Yalla in May 2021.

title: A factory supplying Samsung received recruiting help from Xinjiang in 2023
points: The New York Times reported that Transimage had received help recruiting workers from a labor dispatch center in Akqi County, Xinjiang, in 2023.
Their investigation found that these programs were much more extensive than previously known.
The latest dated finding concerned the May 29, 2025 investigation by The New York Times and its reporting partners.
body: Jiangsu Chuanyi Technology Company Ltd., also known as Transimage, is a Chinese company linked to Samsung's supply chain. The available reporting did not describe what the company told investors about its workforce or recruitment practices.
On May 29, 2025, The New York Times reported that Transimage had received help recruiting workers from a labor dispatch center in Akqi County, Xinjiang, in 2023.

The New York Times, the Bureau of Investigative Journalism and Der Spiegel jointly investigated state-led programs that moved Uyghur workers from Xinjiang to factories across China. Their investigation found that these programs were much more extensive than previously known. Transimage was among the companies named in the reporting.

The investigation raised questions about forced labor in supply chains serving global brands. Samsung said it had found no evidence of forced labor at Jiangsu Chuanyi Technology. Samsung also said it prohibited suppliers from using any form of forced labor.

The latest dated finding concerned the May 29, 2025 investigation by The New York Times and its reporting partners. It documented recruiting assistance involving a Xinjiang labor dispatch center in 2023, while Samsung disputed the implication that forced labor had occurred at the company.

investigator: BMF Reports, Spruce Point Capital Management
title: Only 2% of Tempus revenue came from AI while short sellers questioned stock value
points: The reports said a joint venture between Japan's SoftBank and Tempus appeared to involve round-tripping capital to create revenue and income.
Both firms estimated a 50% to 60% potential downside for the shares, and the stock tumbled after the revenue sources were questioned.
An earlier report by Two Natural Cap highlighted that Tempus earned about 1% of its 2023 revenue from AI offerings.
body: Tempus AI is a healthcare technology company that told investors it provides AI-enabled precision medicine solutions.

On May 27, 2025, BMF Reports published a report stating that the company relies on open-source models and recycled genomics tools. On May 28, 2025, Spruce Point Capital Management also published a report alleging that the company engages in aggressive accounting practices and that only 2% of revenue stems from AI applications.

The reports said a joint venture between Japan's SoftBank and Tempus appeared to involve round-tripping capital to create revenue and income. Both firms estimated a 50% to 60% potential downside for the shares, and the stock tumbled after the revenue sources were questioned.
An earlier report by Two Natural Cap highlighted that Tempus earned about 1% of its 2023 revenue from AI offerings.

title: Karnataka Bank executives spent past their limits. The board refused to approve it.
points: Independent analyst Hemindra Hazari reviewed the notes in the bank's fourth-quarter financial results and questioned the company.
In response to Hazari's query, the bank acknowledged that the unratified appointee had resigned.
Karnataka Bank informed stock exchanges that both executives had resigned, citing personal reasons, and the shares fell 6%.
body: Karnataka Bank Limited is a century-old regional private sector bank in India that had hired outside leadership. Chief executive Srikrishnan Hari Hara Sarma and executive director Sekhar Rao had joined the bank in 2023.

On May 23, 2025, independent analyst Hemindra Hazari reviewed the notes in the bank's fourth-quarter financial results and questioned the company. He reported that the two executives spent money beyond their designated powers and made an unapproved appointment.
The bank's board refused to ratify the expenses and demanded reimbursement from the executives. In response to Hazari's query, the bank acknowledged that the unratified appointee had resigned.

On June 29, 2025, Karnataka Bank informed stock exchanges that both executives had resigned, citing personal reasons, and the shares fell 6%. On September 22, 2026, Hazari reported that the Reserve Bank of India denied variable pay to the former executives over governance concerns.

title: A short seller warned an FBI probe could cost Marqeta 70% of its business
points: The report alleged that an FBI investigation into Marqeta's banking partner, Sutton Bank, for potential anti-money laundering failures could cause Marqeta to lose up to 70% of its business.

It also said Marqeta's largest client, Block's Cash App, redefined their relationship in 2023 and cut Marqeta's gross profit per dollar transaction, while contracted backlog declined since the first quarter of 2024.
Marqeta shares fell 7% on May 22, 2025 following the report.
body: Marqeta is a US-listed payment processor that relies on partnerships with smaller banks for its Banking as a Service model. It pointed investors to its contracted backlog as an indicator of future revenue.

On May 22, 2025, J Capital Research published a report based on publicly available information and interviews with fintech experts and former executives. The firm held a short position in Marqeta, meaning it earns when the shares fall.

The report alleged that an FBI investigation into Marqeta's banking partner, Sutton Bank, for potential anti-money laundering failures could cause Marqeta to lose up to 70% of its business. It also said Marqeta's largest client, Block's Cash App, redefined their relationship in 2023 and cut Marqeta's gross profit per dollar transaction, while contracted backlog declined since the first quarter of 2024.
Marqeta shares fell 7% on May 22, 2025 following the report.

title: Lottery.com claimed $250 million in loans. A short seller set its price target at zero.
points: It said the two named lenders could not lend $250 million, and that the higher cash on hand came from stock dilution.
One report noted the shares were up 0.74% and that the SEC had recently sent the company a delisting notice.
Lawsuits against the company also remained ongoing, including a claim from a California church that it was defrauded of $2.7 million.
body: Lottery.com is a United States company listed under the ticker LTRY. It reported increased cash on hand and said two entities, Generating Alpha LTD and United Capital Investments London, could lend it $250 million.

On May 21, 2025, short seller Ragnarok Research published a report and said it held a short position, meaning it earns when the shares fall. The firm examined the company's financials and set a price target of zero.

Ragnarok Research alleged that Lottery.com had closed its main operations since mid-2022 and made revenue through subsidiaries engaged in illegal or fraudulent activity. It said the two named lenders could not lend $250 million, and that the higher cash on hand came from stock dilution.

On May 22, 2025, one report noted the shares were up 0.74% and that the SEC had recently sent the company a delisting notice. Lawsuits against the company also remained ongoing, including a claim from a California church that it was defrauded of $2.7 million.

title: Archer promised to fly at the Dubai Airshow. Its air taxi sat static instead.
points: Hunterbrook Media published a report stating that Hunterbrook Capital held a short position in the company.
Hunterbrook geolocated footage of the flight test and reported that the Midnight sat static at the Dubai Airshow while the test took place at Al Ain International Airport, over 50 miles away.
Archer did not say why and did not respond.
body: Archer Aviation is a publicly traded electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft company in the United States that told investors it would fly its flagship Midnight electric air taxi at the 2025 Dubai Airshow.

On June 26, 2026, Hunterbrook Media published a report stating that Hunterbrook Capital held a short position in the company. Hunterbrook geolocated footage of the flight test and reported that the Midnight sat static at the Dubai Airshow while the test took place at Al Ain International Airport, over 50 miles away.
Archer did not say why and did not respond.
Hunterbrook reported that Archer's model sat static at the Dubai Airshow.

title: A short seller said Main Street Capital inflated its portfolio values.
points: Jehoshaphat Research alleged that Main Street Capital had been systematically inflating the fair values of its investment portfolio.
News reports on May 14 and May 15, 2025, noted the short seller saw a likely dividend cut.
The latest report on May 15, 2025, repeated the allegation that Main Street Capital faced a likely dividend cut.
body: Main Street Capital is a business development company that trades under the ticker MAIN. In the first quarter of 2025, it reported $1.01 in distributable net investment income, compared with a consensus estimate of $1.02.

On May 11, 2025, Jehoshaphat Research published a report on Main Street Capital. The firm stated it held a short position in the stock, meaning it earns when the shares fall, and noted short interest was 4%.

Jehoshaphat Research alleged that Main Street Capital had been systematically inflating the fair values of its investment portfolio. News reports on May 14 and May 15, 2025, noted the short seller saw a likely dividend cut.
The latest report on May 15, 2025, repeated the allegation that Main Street Capital faced a likely dividend cut.

title: Aurora pitched a $200 billion market. Short sellers valued it at $10 billion.
points: Short seller Bleecker Street Research published a report saying it held a short position in Aurora, earning when the shares fell.
It said a senior executive at partner Volvo put mass production closer to 2030 and estimated Aurora would need $2-3 billion rather than the ~$750 million it claimed.

Based on talks with employees at partners Volvo and PACCAR, Kerrisdale alleged autonomous trucks would cost about 50% more than manned ones and estimated the viable market at about 17 billion miles, or $8.5 billion to $10 billion.
body: Aurora Innovation is a US autonomous trucking company that told investors it could address a 200 billion mile market. Management projected it could charge $0.65-0.85 per mile and deploy more than 10,000 revenue-generating trucks by the end of 2027.

On May 14, 2025, short seller Bleecker Street Research published a report saying it held a short position in Aurora, earning when the shares fell. It said a senior executive at partner Volvo put mass production closer to 2030 and estimated Aurora would need $2-3 billion rather than the ~$750 million it claimed.

On August 19, 2025, Kerrisdale Capital published a report, also disclosing a short position. Based on talks with employees at partners Volvo and PACCAR, Kerrisdale alleged autonomous trucks would cost about 50% more than manned ones and estimated the viable market at about 17 billion miles, or $8.5 billion to $10 billion.

Bleecker Street Research also reported that co-founder Sterling Anderson had left as Chief Product Officer and Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi left the board in January, while Uber announced $1.0 billion of 2028 notes exchangeable into Aurora shares.

title: Mercurity was valued at $399 million. Its revenue was nearly zero, a short seller said.
points: The short seller said Mercurity traded at 383 times enterprise value to sales.
Morpheus said Mercurity's CEO and CFO had been arrested in China in 2022 and its digital assets seized.
It cited an August 2022 special committee recommendation to suspend Yang Jie after an earlier Hindenburg report.
body: Mercurity Fintech Holding is a New York-based company focused on cryptocurrency mining, AI infrastructure and financial services. Its shares traded near four-year highs following company announcements. Morpheus Research said the business generated virtually no revenue despite its $399 million market value.

On May 8, 2025, Morpheus Research published a report alleging that Mercurity had spent a decade pursuing failed business initiatives and was now promoting AI hardware, fintech and blockchain. The short seller said Mercurity traded at 383 times enterprise value to sales. Morpheus disclosed a short position, meaning it earned when the shares fell.

Morpheus said Mercurity's CEO and CFO had been arrested in China in 2022 and its digital assets seized. It cited an August 2022 special committee recommendation to suspend Yang Jie after an earlier Hindenburg report. Morpheus also visited a purported address of Yingke Precision and reported finding no references on that floor to Yingke Precision, Mercurity, Aifinity or ZJK.
On June 20, 2025, US~Observer reported it was investigating Morpheus Research's own short-selling tactics, including questions about its funding, trading and report validity.

title: Short sellers targeted Nexstar Media Group. Its shares later rose 43.28%.
points: Two days later, on May 2, 2025, short seller BMF Reports published its own report alleging that Nexstar was masking a decline through acquisitions, outdated technology, and financial engineering.
BMF Reports alleged that Nexstar insiders sold over $48 million in shares over six months while the company continued aggressive share buybacks to support metrics and investor sentiment.
At the time BMF Reports wrote its report, Nexstar shares traded at $149.42.
body: Nexstar Media Group, Inc. is listed on Nasdaq and is the largest local television broadcaster in the United States. The company owns or provides services to over 200 stations in nearly 120 markets, along with 138 websites and 229 apps, and presents itself as a modern, digitally scaled media business.

On April 30, 2025, Grizzly Research published a report saying Nexstar was failing with its digital strategy. Two days later, on May 2, 2025, short seller BMF Reports published its own report alleging that Nexstar was masking a decline through acquisitions, outdated technology, and financial engineering.

BMF Reports alleged that Nexstar insiders sold over $48 million in shares over six months while the company continued aggressive share buybacks to support metrics and investor sentiment. At the time BMF Reports wrote its report, Nexstar shares traded at $149.42.

title: Backblaze capitalized 9.8% to 14.4% of revenue in software costs each year
points: The firm reviewed financial statements and compared Backblaze against 42 software peers.
Morpheus Research alleged that Backblaze capitalized software development costs equal to 9.8% to 14.4% of revenue each year since 2022, nearly five times the peer average.
Backblaze denied all the allegations and said Morpheus Research was trying to manipulate its stock price for financial gain.
body: Backblaze is a California cloud storage and backup provider listed on Nasdaq. In Q3 2024, it told investors it would reach positive adjusted free cash flow by Q4 2025.

On April 24, 2025, Morpheus Research published a report on Backblaze and said it held a short position, earning when the shares fall. The firm reviewed financial statements and compared Backblaze against 42 software peers.

Morpheus Research alleged that Backblaze capitalized software development costs equal to 9.8% to 14.4% of revenue each year since 2022, nearly five times the peer average. Drawing on October 2024 lawsuits from two former senior employees, the report also alleged that the CFO sent inflated cash flow forecasts to auditors in 2023 and that founders sold 10,000 shares a day after the April 2022 lock-up expired.
On April 29, 2025, Backblaze denied all the allegations and said Morpheus Research was trying to manipulate its stock price for financial gain.

title: NIO's ONVO deliveries fell 51.7%, pulling the stock to a six-year low
points: In October, NIO delivered 34,246 cars, down 15.2% from the previous year.
Deliveries for ONVO, its family brand, dropped 51.7% to 8,383 vehicles and accounted for all of the decline, while the NIO brand grew 5.7%.
NIO scheduled its next earnings report for December 1, 2026.
body: NIO Inc. is a Cayman Islands holding company with American depositary shares listed on the New York Stock Exchange. It has no equity ownership in its consolidated variable interest entities in China, including Beijing NIO Network Technology Co., Ltd. The company told investors its fourth-quarter goal was more than 40,000 vehicle deliveries a month.

In October, NIO delivered 34,246 cars, down 15.2% from the previous year. Deliveries for ONVO, its family brand, dropped 51.7% to 8,383 vehicles and accounted for all of the decline, while the NIO brand grew 5.7%.

To meet its fourth-quarter target, NIO needed about 42,900 deliveries in each of November and December. Earlier, in its second-quarter 2026 earnings report, the company posted revenue of $32.14 billion and adjusted earnings per share of -$0.29, and shares fell 4.37% to $4.045.
By November 19, 2026, NIO shares had fallen 15% in a week and touched a six-year low. NIO scheduled its next earnings report for December 1, 2026.

title: A short seller questioned Monster's accounting after a 2023 auditor change
points: The report alleged that consumers were shifting toward healthier energy and hydration drinks, slowing Monster's growth in the US and Canada.
Spruce Point also alleged concerns with Monster's financial reporting and accounting choices after the company changed auditors in 2023.
The company said the report contained false and misleading characterizations from non-credible sources and stated it would not comment further.
body: Monster Beverage Corporation is a holding company based in Corona, California, and listed on Nasdaq. Through its subsidiaries, it markets and distributes energy drinks and alcoholic beverages.

On April 8, 2025, short-selling firm Spruce Point Capital Management published a report and issued a strong sell opinion on Monster following a forensic financial review. The report alleged that consumers were shifting toward healthier energy and hydration drinks, slowing Monster's growth in the US and Canada.

Spruce Point also alleged concerns with Monster's financial reporting and accounting choices after the company changed auditors in 2023. The report further claimed Monster had failed to separate the duties of its chief financial officer, chief accounting officer, and chief operating officer roles, and faced unsustainable international growth.

On April 9, 2025, Monster issued a statement denying the claims. The company said the report contained false and misleading characterizations from non-credible sources and stated it would not comment further.

title: Doximity claimed 80% of US doctors. Investigators said it scraped a database.
points: Marketing staff from top pharmaceutical firms also described contract delivery patterns, impression throttling, and gaps between claimed and actual engagement.
Doximity shares traded below their 2021 initial public offering price of $26.
Doximity raised its full-year revenue guidance to $678 million to $683 million and reported $713 million in liquidity.
body: Doximity is a publicly traded online network for healthcare professionals that makes money by letting pharmaceutical companies target doctors with ads. It told investors it reached over 80% of U.S. physicians.

On March 30, 2025, short seller The Captain's Log highlighted research by independent analyst Lauren Balik on Doximity. Balik alleged that Doximity scraped the NPI database to pre-populate profiles for every U.S. physician, pressured doctors into claiming them, and pulled forward revenue on large accounts as smaller customers churned.

In December 2025, physician writer kianimd published an analysis building on Balik and Jehoshaphat Research, noting Doximity faced a securities lawsuit over the allegedly misleading active-member metric. Marketing staff from top pharmaceutical firms also described contract delivery patterns, impression throttling, and gaps between claimed and actual engagement.

By August 18, 2026, Doximity shares traded below their 2021 initial public offering price of $26. On November 11, 2026, Doximity raised its full-year revenue guidance to $678 million to $683 million and reported $713 million in liquidity.

title: ODDITY Tech claimed to be online-only while operating 43 stores
points: The firm said a three-month on-the-ground investigation used dozens of interviews and thousands of documents to check the company.
NINGI Research alleged that ODDITY Tech owned and operated 43 brick-and-mortar retail stores through a subsidiary called Il Makiage Beauty rather than running an online-only business.
The report also alleged that insiders and backers sold over $400 million of stock at the IPO and said the company relied on dishonest marketing tactics and hundreds of undisclosed lawsuits.
body: ODDITY Tech Ltd. is an Israeli beauty and wellness company listed on Nasdaq under the ticker ODD. It launched its Il Makiage cosmetics brand in 2013 and its SpoiledChild skincare brand in 2022. The company told investors it ran a 100 percent digital business model.

On May 21, 2024, short seller NINGI Research published a report on ODDITY Tech and said it was short the stock. The firm said a three-month on-the-ground investigation used dozens of interviews and thousands of documents to check the company.

NINGI Research alleged that ODDITY Tech owned and operated 43 brick-and-mortar retail stores through a subsidiary called Il Makiage Beauty rather than running an online-only business. The report also alleged that insiders and backers sold over $400 million of stock at the IPO and said the company relied on dishonest marketing tactics and hundreds of undisclosed lawsuits.
Both NINGI Research and The Nexus Files had published reports challenging ODDITY Tech's growth narrative and valuation.

title: Gotham City said Kyndryl overstated adjusted EBITDA by 61% to 72%
points: The firm interviewed an industry consultant and reviewed Kyndryl's accounting since 2023, when Kyndryl stopped reporting its costs to IBM.
It calculated that adjusted EBITDA was 61% to 72% lower if costs were capitalized in line with peers, and warned of higher IBM costs.
Kyndryl shares fell nearly 13% on March 27, 2025.
body: Kyndryl is an IT services and consulting provider spun off from IBM. It told investors that growth in consulting would offset declines in legacy mainframe services.

On March 27, 2025, short seller Gotham City Research published a report on the company, earning when the shares fall. The firm interviewed an industry consultant and reviewed Kyndryl's accounting since 2023, when Kyndryl stopped reporting its costs to IBM.

Gotham City alleged that Kyndryl shifted managed service accounts into consulting to create an illusion of growth and manipulated adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow. It calculated that adjusted EBITDA was 61% to 72% lower if costs were capitalized in line with peers, and warned of higher IBM costs.
Kyndryl shares fell nearly 13% on March 27, 2025. A Kyndryl spokesperson rejected the report's conclusions as inaccurate and designed to manipulate the stock for the short seller's benefit.
On March 28, 2025, Gotham City published a follow-up report stating that Kyndryl was trying to mislead people.

title: Vita Coco faced a $90 million revenue threat from one Costco contract
points: BMF examined retail sales data and estimated that the contract represented up to $90 million in annual revenue, nearly 25% of Vita Coco's 2023 total.
NINGI predicted a $90 million revenue shortfall by the end of 2025.
BMF alleged that Costco had already dropped Vita Coco in 2024 and that the company had not disclosed the loss.
body: The Vita Coco Company sells coconut water and other drinks in the United States. It presented itself to investors as a growing beverage business with a strong supply chain and expanding product lines. Its private-label operation also produced coconut water for retailers, including Costco.

On March 26, 2025, short sellers NINGI Research and BMF Reports published separate reports alleging that Vita Coco was losing its Costco business. NINGI examined import records and said Costco was moving Kirkland coconut water production to a competitor. BMF examined retail sales data and estimated that the contract represented up to $90 million in annual revenue, nearly 25% of Vita Coco's 2023 total.

NINGI predicted a $90 million revenue shortfall by the end of 2025. BMF alleged that Costco had already dropped Vita Coco in 2024 and that the company had not disclosed the loss. NINGI also alleged undisclosed related-party transactions and inventory shortages. NINGI held a short position, which would benefit if Vita Coco's shares fell.

On March 27, NINGI published a follow-up criticizing Vita Coco's rebuttal. It reported that supplier Ducoco, responsible for 8.5% of Vita Coco's supply, had sought bankruptcy protection in February 2025 with $118 million in debt. NINGI said Vita Coco had not addressed that bankruptcy on its earnings calls.

title: Hesai told US courts it had no military ties. Short sellers pointed to state TV.
points: Hesai shares came under pressure that day.
Hesai issued a statement in response saying it was aware of the Blue Orca Capital report.

Short seller BMF Reports published its own report when Hesai shares traded at $22.30, saying a former Hesai employee confirmed witnessing production for military applications at the company's Shanghai facilities.
body: Hesai Group is a Nasdaq-listed maker of three-dimensional light detection and ranging (lidar) sensors with offices in Shanghai, Palo Alto and Stuttgart. In January 2024, the U.S. Department of Defense placed Hesai on a list of Chinese military companies, and Hesai sued to be removed from it.

On March 18, 2025, short seller Blue Orca Capital published a report and said it was short the stock, meaning it earns when the shares fall. Blue Orca alleged that Hesai lied to investors, U.S. authorities and the court about military use of its lidar technology, citing images from Chinese state-owned CCTV that appeared to show a Chinese military vehicle with a Hesai lidar system.
Hesai shares came under pressure that day. On March 19, 2025, Hesai issued a statement in response saying it was aware of the Blue Orca Capital report.

On March 24, 2025, short seller BMF Reports published its own report when Hesai shares traded at $22.30, saying a former Hesai employee confirmed witnessing production for military applications at the company's Shanghai facilities.

title: Appian sold compliance software while its key European client stayed in Russia
points: The report cited a February Bloomberg article stating Russia held €4.4 billion of Raiffeisen Bank's profits and that the bank financed Russian military suppliers.
Full-year 2025 revenue reached $726.9 million, up from $617.0 million in 2024, and the company recorded its first full year of GAAP net income.
Appian had also won a US Army agreement worth up to $500 million over ten years.
body: Appian Corporation is a US software company listed on Nasdaq that sells low-code business automation tools to large enterprises and federal agencies.

On March 18, 2025, short seller The Captain's Log published a report alleging that a large share of Appian's European revenue and operations came from Austrian lender Raiffeisen Bank. The report said Raiffeisen Bank built compliance processes on Appian's software through a Kosovo spin-off called Raiffeisen Tech while operating in Russia and facing criticism over anti-money laundering standards.

The report cited a February Bloomberg article stating Russia held €4.4 billion of Raiffeisen Bank's profits and that the bank financed Russian military suppliers. On March 23, 2025, independent researcher Lauren Balik repeated the allegation in The Bear Cave newsletter.

Appian's business later grew rather than collapsed. Full-year 2025 revenue reached $726.9 million, up from $617.0 million in 2024, and the company recorded its first full year of GAAP net income. By July 21, 2026, Appian had also won a US Army agreement worth up to $500 million over ten years.

title: Solaris said its turbine unit was diversified. Its 10-K showed 96% came from xAI.
points: The report said Solaris paid $60 million in cash, about 16.5 million shares, and paid off $71 million in debt for turbines worth $54.7 million.
The report cited the company's 10-K filing showing that 96% of turbine leasing revenue during 2024 came from Elon Musk's xAI.
Shares of Solaris fell 17% on March 17, 2025, following the research note.
body: Solaris Energy Infrastructure is a $1.65 billion Houston-based mobile power and oilfield services company. In July 2024, it announced a plan to buy Mobile Energy Rentals, telling investors the business had a diversified earnings stream and recognized industry leaders.

On March 17, 2025, short-selling firm Morpheus Research published a report on X targeting Solaris. The report said Solaris paid $60 million in cash, about 16.5 million shares, and paid off $71 million in debt for turbines worth $54.7 million.

Morpheus Research alleged that co-owners John Tuma and John Johnson turned those turbines into cash and stock worth about $246 million at closing and closer to $460 million by the report date. The report cited the company's 10-K filing showing that 96% of turbine leasing revenue during 2024 came from Elon Musk's xAI.
Shares of Solaris fell 17% on March 17, 2025, following the research note. That drop was the largest single-day decline for the stock since January.

title: Brokerage commission jumped three-fold at PB Fintech. The CEO called the impact minimal.
points: Trudence Capital alleged that total commission paid to insurance distributors rose sharply after March 2023.
The report stated that PB Fintech's brokerage commission earned jumped three-fold in FY24, which differed from what management told investors on earnings calls.
Separately, in March 2025, founder and chairman Yashish Dahiya won a settlement order from the Securities and Exchange Board of India.
body: PB Fintech is an Indian financial company that runs the lending arm Paisabazaar. On post-earnings calls in Q4FY23 and Q1 FY24, CEO Yashish Dahiya told analysts that commission changes had a minimal impact on revenue and that the take rate had no material shifts.

In March 2025, Mumbai-based forensic research firm Trudence Capital published a report titled 'Premium Promises and Discounted Truths'. The report questioned PB Fintech's past revenue recognition practices and the role of Paisabazaar.

Trudence Capital alleged that total commission paid to insurance distributors rose sharply after March 2023. The report stated that PB Fintech's brokerage commission earned jumped three-fold in FY24, which differed from what management told investors on earnings calls.

Separately, in March 2025, founder and chairman Yashish Dahiya won a settlement order from the Securities and Exchange Board of India. That case involved allegedly suppressing price-sensitive information about an overseas acquisition from the stock exchanges.

title: Unplugged cables at the border. OSI Systems booked $343 million on a $612 million contract.
points: Culper said its investigators visited border crossings in Mexico in February 2024 and checked Google Earth.
At Reynosa, investigators found seven light vehicle systems and two cargo systems blocked off with ropes, caution tape, or barriers, with cables unplugged and loose equipment on the ground.
Soren Aandahl of Blue Orca Capital presented a short pitch on OSI Systems at the Sohn New York Conference.
body: OSI Systems is a United States designer and manufacturer of electronic security, screening, and inspection systems listed on Nasdaq. On January 17, 2023, it announced an award of over $200 million for cargo and vehicle inspection systems, part of a $612 million contract including $424 million in product and installation revenues.

On March 13, 2025, short seller Culper Research published a report on the company and said it held a short position, earning when the shares fall. Culper estimated OSI had recognized $343 million in revenues through the second quarter of 2025, while insiders sold $83.7 million in stock over three years and $40.8 million in the past year.

Culper said its investigators visited border crossings in Mexico in February 2024 and checked Google Earth. At Reynosa, investigators found seven light vehicle systems and two cargo systems blocked off with ropes, caution tape, or barriers, with cables unplugged and loose equipment on the ground.
On May 12, 2026, Soren Aandahl of Blue Orca Capital presented a short pitch on OSI Systems at the Sohn New York Conference. The pitch focused on revenue recognition and cash collection.

title: XP said a short seller's report caused over $100 million in harm and sued
points: XP said it suffered more than $100 million in harm to its business and reputation, with longtime clients, investors, and business partners withdrawing funds.
XP also asked authorities to investigate criminal claims against Grizzly CEO Siegfried Eggert in Brazil.
Grizzly Research issued a public statement standing behind its report and its accuracy.
body: XP Inc. is a Brazilian financial services company centered on investment management, advisory, and digital financial services. It is listed on Nasdaq.

On March 12, 2025, short seller Grizzly Research published a report titled "XP's (Nasdaq: XP) Entire Profits Are Dependent on What Insiders Call a 'Madoff-Like Ponzi Scheme'." Grizzly Research said its report was based on generally available information, field research, inferences, and deductions.

On July 7, 2025, XP filed a defamation lawsuit against Grizzly Research in federal court in Manhattan. XP said it suffered more than $100 million in harm to its business and reputation, with longtime clients, investors, and business partners withdrawing funds. XP also asked authorities to investigate criminal claims against Grizzly CEO Siegfried Eggert in Brazil.

On November 21, 2025, Grizzly Research issued a public statement standing behind its report and its accuracy. It stated that its affiliates held a short position in XP Inc., meaning they earn when the shares fall.

title: A $35 billion AI server maker re-hired executives from a 2018 accounting issue
points: The report also alleged that Super Micro Computer re-hired top executives who were directly involved in a previous accounting issue that led to a temporary Nasdaq delisting in 2018.
By the time of the news report, the stock had fallen 55% from its March all-time high to $547.64.
Those indicted included a Super Micro Computer board member named in the Hindenburg report and another company manager.
body: Super Micro Computer is a US technology company that makes artificial intelligence servers. A partnership with Nvidia helped it capitalize on surging demand for those servers, lifting its market value to $35 billion.

In August 2024, Hindenburg Research published a report on the company and stated it held a short position, earning when the shares fall. Hindenburg said it found evidence of accounting manipulation, undisclosed related party transactions, and sanction and export control failures in China and Russia.
